  - id: J30e07edea4458b0b
    okf_path: OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol1/secC.md
    okf_sha256: 5ae5ea7a30496ffbb3384dfb998e3fdd89ef3222744b6b639e3d564508b11172
    heading: Clause 2.0 — Eligible Tenderers
    source_document: Vol1DLNP1.pdf
    source_sha256: 74441e621d2e627d9132506a894883aff3b5fe3fdfa9600f5be3c7ec394d5c5c
    pdf_pages:
    - 27
    - 28
    - 29
    - 30
    - 31
    sheet_cells: ''
    json_path: parsed_json/vol1/section_c_eqc/eqc_clauses.json
    json_sha256: d8207622663bc2dd0cf2a7c5e3ed660f5c3881838e376d1bbb26fdae47ed8abf
    json_pointer: /clauses/1
    json_record_id: null
    source_review_status: pending_manual_review
    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"2.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 27,\n      \"text\": \"\
      2.0     ELIGIBLE TENDERERS\\n\\n\\n       2.1.   Tenderer may be a Proprietorship Firm/ Partnership Firm/Private\
      \ Limited Company/ Public\\n              Limited Company. Tenderer shall apply as a Single Entity. Joint\
      \ Venture/Consortium is\\n            not permitted in this tender.\\n\\n       2.2.   Only those Tenderers\
      \ who satisfy the condition of ‘Class-I Local Supplier’ as per Clause\\n              2.3 of EQC shall be\
      \ eligible to participate in this Tender.\\n\\n       2.3.    ‘Class-I Local Supplier’ means a supplier or\
      \ service provider whose goods, services or works\\n              offered for procurement, meets the minimum\
      \ Local content of 90%.\\n\\n       2.4.    ‘Local content’ means the amount of value added in India which\
      \ shall, be the total value of\\n              the item procured (excluding net domestic indirect taxes) minus\
      \ the value of imported content\\n                 in the item (including all customs duties) as proportion\
      \ of the total value, in percent.\\n\\n       2.5.   The minimum Local Content for this service shall be certified\
      \ as below;\\n\\n                (a) The ‘Class-I Local Supplier’ at the time of Bid submission shall provide\
      \ a Declaration\\n                    that the item offered meets the minimum ‘Local Content’ and shall give\
      \ details of the\\n                    location(s) at which the local value addition is made. (Attachment-1\
      \ to Letter of Technical\\n                    Bid).\\n\\n                (b) DELETED\\n\\n       2.6.   Bidder\
      \ claiming as ‘Class-I Local Supplier is exempted from meeting the stipulated\\n             ‘Local content’\
      \ in case, if the product is being manufactured in India under a license from a\\n               foreign manufacturer,\
      \ who holds intellectual property rights and where there is a technology\\n               collaboration agreement/transfer\

      n              Declarations by the Bidder may be constituted by BMRCL on random basis and in case of\\n  \

      \ any person or firm or company, including any member of a consortium or joint\\n                venture (that\

      \ person not falling in any of the descriptions of Bidders stated hereinbefore,\\n                  including\

      \ or\\n\\n                     (c) An  entity  substantially  controlled through  entities  incorporated,\

      \    iii. The beneficial owner for the purpose of (ii) above will be as under:\\n\\n                    (a)\
      \ In case of a company or Limited Liability Partnership, the beneficial owner is the\\n                  \

      \         juridical person, has a controlling ownership interest or who exercises control through\\n     \
      \                other means.\\n\\n                         \\\"Controlling ownership interest\\\" means\

      \ capital or profits of the company;\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 29,\n      \"text\": \"   \\\"\
      Control” shall include the right to appoint majority of the directors or to control\\n                   \
      \      the management or policy decisions including by virtue of their shareholding or\\n                \
      \    management rights or shareholders  agreements  or voting agreements;\\n                    (b) In case\
      \ of a partnership firm, the beneficial owner is the natural person(s) who,\\n                   whether acting\
      \ alone or together, or through one or more juridical person, has\\n                   ownership of entitlement\
      \ to more than fifteen percent of capital or profits of the\\n                      partnership;\\n\\n   \
      \                  (c) In case of an unincorporated association or body of individuals, the beneficial owner\\\
      n                           is the natural person(s), who, whether acting alone or together, or through one\
      \ or\\n                 more juridical person, has ownership of or entitlement to more than fifteen percent\
      \ of\\n                     the property or capital or profits of such association or body of individuals;\\\
      n\\n                    (d) Where no natural person is identified under (a) or (b) or (c) above, the beneficial\\\
      n                  owner is the relevant natural person who holds the position of senior managing\\n     \
      \                       official;\\n\\n                    (e) In case of a trust, the identification  of\
      \ beneficial  owner(s) shall include identification\\n                       of the author of the trust, the\
      \ trustee, the beneficiaries with fifteen percent or more\\n                        interest in the trust\
      \ and any other natural person exercising ultimate effective control\\n                    over the trust\
      \ through a chain of control or ownership.\\n\\n                         (f) An Agent is a person employed\
      \ to do any act for another, or to represent another in\\n                     dealings with third person.\\\
      n\\n                                      i. Successful Bidder shall not be allowed to sub-contract works\
      \ to any contractor from\\n                  a country which shares a land border with India unless such contractor\
      \ is registered\\n                       with the Competent Authority. The definition of “Contractor from\

      n                                       ii. The registration shall be valid at the time of submission of bids\
      \ and at the time of\\n                    acceptance of bid.\\n                                       iii.\
      \ If the bidder was validly registered at the time of acceptance / placement of order,\\n                \
      \         registration shall not be relevant consideration during contract execution.\\n       2.11.  Bidder\
      \  is required  to submit undertaking  for compliance  of the above Clause 2.10\\n             (Attachment-1\
      \ to Letter of Technical Bid).\\n\\n       2.12.  The above Clause 2.10 will not apply to Bidders from those\

      \ Updated lists of countries to\\n             which lines of credit have been extended or in which development\
      \ projects are undertaken\\n             are given in the website of the Ministry of External Affairs.\\n\\\
      n       2.13.  Tenderers shall not have a conflict of interest that affects the Bidding Process. Any Tenderer\\\
      n             found to have a Conflict of Interest shall be disqualified. A Tenderer will be deemed to have\\\
      n               Conflict of interest with one or more parties in this Tendering process, if:\\n\\n       \
      \         (a) A tenderer submits more than one bid either individually or as a member of a JV for a\\n   \

      \ The Tenderer has been engaged by the Employer to provide consulting services for the\\n                \

      \ (inclusive of parent firms) of the Bidder has been engaged by\\n                  the Employer to provide\

      \      \"text\": \"for or implementation of this work.\\n\\n                (d) The Tenderer lends, or temporarily\

      \ for the preparation related to procurement for\\n                   or implementation of this work.\\n\\\
      n       2.14.  DELETED\\n\\n       2.15.  As on date of submission of Bid, the Bidder (each member, in case\
      \ of JV) should not be\\n             excluded as per the GROUNDS FOR EXCLUSION. The Bidder should submit\
      \ an\\n              undertaking to this effect.\\n\\n                      (i) GROUNDS FOR EXCLUSION will\

      \ committed during the procurement or performance of a\\n                     contract, unless they provide\

      \          (d) have not fulfilled their obligations regarding the payment of social security contributions\\\
      n                    or taxes in accordance with the legal provisions of the country where they are\\n   \
      \                 established or the Employer ‘s country;\\n\\n                  (e) have indulged in ‘Corrupt\
      \ Practice’; “corrupt practice” means the offering, giving,\\n                    receiving or soliciting\
      \ of anything of value to influence the action of a public official in\\n                   the procurement\
      \ process or in contract execution;\\n\\n                       (f) have indulged in ‘Fraudulent Practice’;\
      \ “fraudulent practice” means a misrepresentation\\n                      of facts in order to influence an\
      \ evaluation process or the execution of a contract, and\\n                    includes misleading or false\
      \ representation in forms or statements or attachment\\n                   submitted and collusive practices\
      \ among Bidders (prior to or after bid submission)\\n                  designed to establish bid prices at\
      \ artificial, non-competitive levels and to deprive the\\n                 Employer of the benefits of free\
      \ and open competitions;\\n\\n                  (g) have been considered ineligible due to execution of Bid–Securing\
      \ Declaration by any\\n                    Central Govt./State Govt./PSUs;\\n\\n                  (h) have\
      \ been Black  listed/debarred /banned business by any Central Govt./State\\n                 Govt./PSUs or\
      \ Local Authority or World Bank or ADB or JICA or any other International\\n                   Financing Institution,\
      \ or any entity controlled by them;\\n\\n                         (i) have left/abandoned the awarded works\
      \ on his own in the last 05 years;\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 31,\n      \"text\": \"(j) “have\

    quote: "{\n  \"pdf_page\": 35,\n  \"text\": \"4) \\nIn case Audited Balance sheet of the last financial year\
      \ ending with 2025-2026 is not made available by the Tenderer, he has to submit \\nan affidavit certifying\
      \ that 'The Balance Sheet has actually not been audited so far'. In such a case the financial data of previous\
      \ '4' \\naudited financial years will be taken into consideration for evaluation. If audited Balance sheet\
      \ of any year other than the last financial \\nyear ending with 2025-2026 is not submitted even when requested\
      \ for as a clarification under clause 20 of ITT, then the Tender will be \\nconsidered as non-responsive.\
      \ \\n5) \\nAll documents shall reflect the stand-alone financial status of the Tenderer and not the Tenderer’s\
      \ parent companies, subsidiaries, or \\naffiliates. \\n6) \\nFor the purpose of evaluation, amounts in foreign\
      \ currencies shall be converted to equivalent INR as per the following procedure: \\nIn cases where the financial\
      \ data is denominated in a currency other than Indian Rupees, it shall be converted into the equivalent value\
      \ \\nin Indian Rupees by adopting the exchange rate between the foreign currency and INR prevailing on the\
      \ last day of the respective \\nfinancial year, as published on the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) website, for\
      \ the purpose of bid evaluation. \\n7) \\nTo align a January–December financial year with the standard April–March\
      \ fiscal year, use the following conversion: \\nA calendar year (e.g., January–December 2023) corresponds\
      \ to the subsequent fiscal year (e.g., FY 2023–24, covering April 2023 to \\nMarch 2024). Apply this rule\
      \ consistently to all such conversions. \\n8) \\n****Financial turnover in INR/converted equivalent INR of\
      \ previous financial years shall be given a weightage of 5% per year \\n(compounded annually) to bring them\
      \ to the price level of the Financial Year of this Tender Invitation. \\n9) \\nAll the documents or certifications,\
      \ which are provided by Chartered Accountant after 1st July, 2019, must contain UDIN thereon and \\nthe particulars\
      \ of certifications must be same as mentioned on document/certification and submitted to ICAI on its website\
      \ which can be \\nverified online on https://udin.icai.org/search-udin. \\n3.2 BID CAPACITY: \\nRequirement\
      \ \\nDocument Submission \\nRequirement \\nAvailable Bid capacity should be ≥ ₹ 4.74 Crores \\nFormula: \\\
      nAvailable Bid Capacity = (1.5 × A × N) – B  \\nAttachment-7, Attachment-\\n8 to Letter of Technical Bid\"\
      \n}"

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"3.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 32,\n      \"text\": \"\
      3.0 \\nQUALIFICATION CRITERIA \\n \\nPursuant to clause 2.0, tenderers shall meet the qualification criteria\
      \ stipulated in the succeeding paragraphs in order to qualify. \\n3.1 WORK EXPERIENCE & FINANCIAL STANDING:\
      \ \\n3.1. A. WORK EXPERIENCE \\nSl. No \\nCriteria Requirement \\nDocument Submission \\nRequirement \\n3.1.A.(i)\
      \ \\nTenderer as a Prime Contractor (Single entity or Joint Venture member) during last 07(seven) \\nyears\
      \ ending as on last day of the month previous to the month of invitation of this tender, \\nshould have completed/\
      \ **substantially completed One work of *Similar nature, where the \\nvalue of the work is equal to or exceed\
      \ ₹ 3.79 Crores.*** \\nAttachment-5 & Attachment-\\n6 to Letter of Technical Bid \\nOR \\n3.1.A. (ii) \\nTenderer\
      \ as a Prime Contractor (Single entity or Joint Venture member) during last 07(seven) \\nyears ending as on\
      \ last day of the month previous to the month of invitation of this tender, \\nshould have completed/ **substantially\
      \ completed Two works of *Similar nature, where the \\nvalue of each work is equal to or exceed ₹ 2.37 Crores.\
      \ *** \\nAttachment-5 & Attachment-\\n6 to Letter of Technical Bid \\nOR \\n3.1.A. (iii) Tenderer as a Prime\
      \ Contractor (Single entity or Joint Venture member) during last 07(seven) \\nyears ending as on last day\
      \ of the month previous to the month of invitation of this tender, \\nshould have completed/ **substantially\
      \ completed Three works of *Similar nature, where the \\nvalue of each work is equal to or exceed ₹ 1.90 Crores.***\
      \ \\nAttachment-5 & Attachment-\\n6 to Letter of Technical Bid \\nOR \\n3.1.A. (iv) Tenderer as a Prime Contractor\
      \ (Single entity or Joint Venture member) during last 07(seven) \\nyears ending as on last day of the month\
      \ previous to the month of invitation of this tender, \\nAttachment-5 & Attachment-\\n6 to Letter of Technical\
      \ Bid\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 33,\n      \"text\": \"should have completed/ **substantially\
      \ completed in any number of works of *Similar nature, \\nwhere the combined value of works is equal to or\
      \ exceed ₹ 4.74 Crores.*** \\nNotes: \\n1) \\n* Similar nature work for this contract shall be, ‘Demolition/Dismantling\
      \ of Buildings/Structures’. \\n2) \\n** Similar nature work(s) where Financial value of physically executed\
      \ work is 90%  or more of the original awarded contract value or \\nrevised contract value (if any), duly\
      \ certified by the client, will be treated as substantially completed Similar nature work(s) and will be \\\
      nconsidered for qualification of work experience criteria. In case original contract value has been revised,\
      \ the revised contract value shall \\nbe considered for this purpose.  \\n3) \\nThe Tenderer shall furnish\
      \ the Client’s Completion Certificate in support of the Work Experience criteria as specified under Clause\
      \ 3.1A. \\nThe certificate shall clearly indicate the Nature and Scope of Similar Nature Work, Awarded Contract\
      \ Value (excluding GST), Actual \\nCompletion Value (excluding GST), and the Actual Date of Completion. Where\
      \ applicable, the certificate shall also specify the Revised \\nContract Value (excluding GST), along with\
      \ details of any variation orders and extensions of time granted. \\n4) \\nIn cases where the Client’s Completion\
      \ Certificate indicates values inclusive of GST and/or other applicable taxes, the Tenderer shall \\nsubmit\
      \ the actual completion cost after deducting the applicable GST dully certified by Chartered Accountant. For\
      \ portions of Similar \\nNature Works executed in the pre-GST period, the Tenderer shall make a deduction\
      \ towards taxes at the rate of 12% to arrive at the \\ncompletion cost exclusive of taxes. \\n5) \\nIf a Tenderer\
      \ has completed /substantially completed the Similar Nature Work(s) as a member of a Joint Venture (JV), the\
      \ value of \\n‘Similar Nature Work(s)’ will be recognized only in proportion to the Tenderer’s stipulated\
      \ financial share in that JV. A copy of the JV \\nAgreement must be submitted with the bid. \\n6) \\nFor the\
      \ purpose of evaluation, value of works in foreign currencies shall be converted to equivalent INR as per\
      \ the following procedure: \\nValue of completed/ substantially completed Similar Nature Work(s) in foreign\
      \ currency shall be converted to Equivalent INR by adopting \\nExchange rate between the foreign currency\
      \ and INR as prevailing on the date of completion / date given in the substantial completion \\ncertificate\
      \ as applicable, as per the website of Reserve Bank of India (RBI). \\n7) \\n***The value of Completed Similar\
      \ Nature Work(s) executed during the previous financial years shall be updated at a rate of 5% per \\nyear,\
      \ compounded annually, for the Indian Rupees portion (including foreign currencies, converted to Equivalent\
      \ INR), to bring them to \\nthe price level of the financial year of this Tender Invitation.\"\n    },\n \
      \   {\n      \"pdf_page\": 34,\n      \"text\": \"The value of ongoing work(s) that are substantially completed\
      \ shall not be updated to the price level of the financial year of this Tender \\nInvitation. \\n8) \\nIn\
      \ case the Similar Nature Work(s) are executed for client other than Government Department, PSU, or other\
      \ Government Body, Contract \\nAgreement, Bill wise details of payment received and Proof of TDS (Form 26AS)\
      \ deducted by clients for all payments received shall be \\nsubmitted duly certified by Chartered Accountant.\
      \ \\n9) \\nWork experience certificates of the tenderers with qualification as a sub-contractor will not be\
      \ considered. \\n3.1. B.  FINANCIAL STANDING: The Tenderer should meet the following financial qualification\
      \ criteria: \\nSl. No \\nCriteria Requirement \\nDocument Submission \\nrequirement \\n3.1.B (i) \\nLiquidity:\
      \ Tenderer shall demonstrate that it has access to, or possess liquid assets and /or \\navailability of credit\
      \ facilities of not less than ₹ 1.19 Crores (Credit lines/ letter of credit/ certificates \\nfrom banks for\
      \ meeting the fund requirement etc.). \\nAttachment-13 to Letter of \\nTechnical Bid \\n3.1.B (ii) \\nAnnual\
      \ Turnover: Tenderer in its name should have in the last five financial years (2021-2022 \\nto 2025-2026)\
      \ achieved in at least two financial years a minimum financial turnover (in all \\nclasses of civil engineering\
      \ construction works only) ≥ ₹ 9.48 Crores. **** \\nAttachment-8 to Letter of \\nTechnical Bid \\n      Notes:\
      \ \\n1) \\nA copy of the Banker’s Certificate issued from a Nationalised / Scheduled Bank in India (for liquidity)\
      \ needs to be uploaded in the \\nTechnical Proposal in respect of EQC Clause 3.1 B (i). \\n2) \\nAnnual financial\
      \ statements (Audited Balance sheets including all related notes and income statements) for last five financial\
      \ years \\n(2021-2022 to 2025-2026) shall be submitted by the Tenderer. The financial information of the Tenderer\
      \ must be certified either by the \\nIndependent Financial Auditor (statutory Auditor) of the company appointed\
      \ under the companies’ Act or by a Chartered Accountant with \\nhis stamp and signature with membership number\
      \ and firm registration number. \\n3) \\nIn case any discrepancy in data is found between the Audited Balance\
      \ sheet and the financial information submitted, the data as available \\nin the Audited Balance sheet will\
      \ be considered.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 35,\n      \"text\": \"4) \\nIn case Audited Balance\
      \ sheet of the last financial year ending with 2025-2026 is not made available by the Tenderer, he has to\
      \ submit \\nan affidavit certifying that 'The Balance Sheet has actually not been audited so far'. In such\
      \ a case the financial data of previous '4' \\naudited financial years will be taken into consideration for\
      \ evaluation. If audited Balance sheet of any year other than the last financial \\nyear ending with 2025-2026\
      \ is not submitted even when requested for as a clarification under clause 20 of ITT, then the Tender will\
      \ be \\nconsidered as non-responsive. \\n5) \\nAll documents shall reflect the stand-alone financial status\
      \ of the Tenderer and not the Tenderer’s parent companies, subsidiaries, or \\naffiliates. \\n6) \\nFor the\
      \ purpose of evaluation, amounts in foreign currencies shall be converted to equivalent INR as per the following\
      \ procedure: \\nIn cases where the financial data is denominated in a currency other than Indian Rupees, it\
      \ shall be converted into the equivalent value \\nin Indian Rupees by adopting the exchange rate between the\
      \ foreign currency and INR prevailing on the last day of the respective \\nfinancial year, as published on\
      \ the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) website, for the purpose of bid evaluation. \\n7) \\nTo align a January–December\
      \ financial year with the standard April–March fiscal year, use the following conversion: \\nA calendar year\
      \ (e.g., January–December 2023) corresponds to the subsequent fiscal year (e.g., FY 2023–24, covering April\
      \ 2023 to \\nMarch 2024). Apply this rule consistently to all such conversions. \\n8) \\n****Financial turnover\
      \ in INR/converted equivalent INR of previous financial years shall be given a weightage of 5% per year \\\
      n(compounded annually) to bring them to the price level of the Financial Year of this Tender Invitation. \\\
      n9) \\nAll the documents or certifications, which are provided by Chartered Accountant after 1st July, 2019,\
      \ must contain UDIN thereon and \\nthe particulars of certifications must be same as mentioned on document/certification\
      \ and submitted to ICAI on its website which can be \\nverified online on https://udin.icai.org/search-udin.\
      \ \\n3.2 BID CAPACITY: \\nRequirement \\nDocument Submission \\nRequirement \\nAvailable Bid capacity should\
      \ be ≥ ₹ 4.74 Crores \\nFormula: \\nAvailable Bid Capacity = (1.5 × A × N) – B  \\nAttachment-7, Attachment-\\\
      n8 to Letter of Technical Bid\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 36,\n      \"text\": \"Requirement \\\
      nDocument Submission \\nRequirement \\nWhere: \\nA = Maximum value of total Civil Engineering works executed\
      \ (annual turnover from Civil Engineering works) \\nin any one year during the last five financial years.\
      \ The turnover for previous years shall be updated by 5% \\nper year (compounded annually) to bring them to\
      \ the price level of the Financial Year of this Tender Invitation.  \\nN = Number of years prescribed for\
      \ completion of this tendered work as mentioned in NIT.  \\nB = Total value (updated to the price level of\
      \ the Financial Year of this Tender Invitation) of existing \\ncommitments for ongoing Civil Engineering works\
      \ during the completion period mentioned in NIT, from the \\nlast day of the month previous to the month of\
      \ invitation of this tender. \\nNotes: \\n1) Works in Hand information provided in ‘Attachment-7 to Letter\
      \ of Technical Bid’ must be certified either by the Independent Financial \\nAuditor (Statutory Auditor) of\
      \ the company appointed under the companies’ Act or by a Chartered Accountant with his stamp and signature\
      \ \\nwith Membership Number and Firm’s Registration Number. \\n2) All the documents or certifications, which\
      \ are provided by Chartered Accountant after 1st July 2019, must contain UDIN thereon and the \\nparticulars\
      \ of certifications must be same as mentioned on document/certification and submitted to ICAI on its website,\
      \ which can be \\nverified online on https://udin.icai.org/search-udin.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"review_status\"\

    quote: "{\n  \"pdf_page\": 49,\n  \"text\": \"ATTACHMENT -8\\n\\n                           Financial Information\
      \ - Updated Annual Turnover\\n\\n     (To be submitted duly signed by tenderer & his Chartered Accountant/\
      \ Independent Financial Auditor)\\n\\n                                    (To be submitted by tenderer)\\\
      n\\n\\n                 Sl.    Financial    Annual Turnover from    Multipl    Updated Annual\\n         \
      \ No     Year            all classes of civil       ying         Turnover\\n                             \
      \       engineering          factor\\n                               construction works only\\n          \
      \                          INR                          INR\\n                                           \
      \        (a)                  (b)             (a)x(b)\\n             1    2021-2022                      \
      \         1.28\\n\\n             2                  2022-2023                               1.22\\n\\n   \
      \          3                  2023-2024                               1.16\\n\\n             4    2024-2025\
      \                               1.10\\n             5    2025-2026                               1.05\\n\\\
      n\\n\\nNote:\\n         1.  Annual  financial statements (Audited Balance sheets including  all related notes\
      \ and income\\n           statements) for last five financial years (2021-22 to 2025-26) shall be submitted\
      \ by the Tenderer.\\n\\n         2.  The financial information/Annual Turnover ( in all classes of civil engineering\
      \ construction works\\n             only) of the Tenderer must be certified either by the Independent Financial\
      \ Auditor (statutory\\n            Auditor) of the company appointed under the Companies’ Act or by a Chartered\
      \ Accountant with his\\n          stamp and signature with membership number and firm registration number.\\\
      n\\n         3.  In case any discrepancy in data is found between the Audited Balance sheet and the financial\\\
      n            information/Annual Turnover (n all classes of civil engineering construction works only) submitted,\\\
      n            the data as available in the Audited Balance sheet will be considered.\\n\\n         4.  In case\
      \ Audited Balance sheet of the last Financial Year ending with 2025-26 is not made available\\n          by\
      \ the Bidder, he must submit an affidavit certifying that 'The Balance Sheet has actually not been\\n    \
      \        audited so far'. In such a case the financial data of previous '4' audited Financial Years will be\
      \ taken\\n              into consideration for evaluation.\\n\\n         5.  To align a January–December financial\
      \ year with the standard April–March fiscal year, use the\\n             following conversion:\\n\\n     \
      \   A calendar year (e.g., January–December 2023) corresponds to the subsequent fiscal year (e.g.,\\n    \
      \     FY 2023–24, covering  April 2023  to March 2024). Apply  this  rule  consistently  to  all such\\n \
      \           conversions.\\n\\n         6.   All documents shall reflect the stand-alone financial status of\
      \ the Tenderer and not the Tenderer’s\\n            parent companies, subsidiaries, or affiliates.\\n\\n \
      \        7.   All the documents or certifications, which are provided by CA after 1st July, 2019, must contain\\\
      n         UDIN  thereon  and  the  particulars  of  certifications  must  be  same  as  mentioned  on\\n \
      \           document/certification and submitted to ICAI on  its website which can be  verified online on\\\
      n             https://udin.icai.org/search-udin.\\n\\n\\n\\n  (Signature) ……………………                       \
      \    (Signature & Seal) ……………………\\n\\n  Name of signatory: ………                     Name of signatory: …………………..\\\
      n\\n  Capacity of signatory: …………………..                  (Chartered Accountant/ Independent Financial Auditor)\\\
      n\\n  Name and address of Tenderer………..                 Address: ……….. UDIN:\"\n}"

      additions to the SCC.'

      \ the Employer shall instruct the other contractors to\\n                        join for the monthly SHE\
      \ committee meeting of the main civil contractor, so as to\\n                   discuss and decide about the\
      \ common provision of security, lighting, toilet, drinking\\n                   water etc. and sharing the\
      \ maintenance cost of the same etc.\\n\\n\\n          7.6.2    The general principle for sharing the cost\
      \ shall be either based on the contract\\n                  value of works executed at the contiguous area\
      \ or the daily average number of\\n               workmen employed by each contractor in the contiguous area.\\\
      n\\n\\n          7.7     Minimum time between two monthly SHE Committee meetings\\n\\n\\n          7.7.1 \
      \   A minimum period of 21 days shall be maintained between any two SHE monthly\\n                  committee\
      \ meetings.\\n\\n\\n          7.8     Agenda\\n\\n\\n          7.8.1    The Secretary shall circulate the\
      \ agenda of the meeting at least seven working days in\\n                 advance of the scheduled date of\
      \ the meeting to all members.\\n\\n\\n          7.8.2    The agenda should broadly cover the following:\\\
      n\\n\\n                                 i)     Confirmation of minutes\\n\\n                             \
      \       ii)    Chairman’s review/overview of site SHE performance / condition\\n\\n                      \
      \               iii)    Previous month SHE statistics\\n\\n                          iv)    Incident and Accident\

      \                       ix)   Matters arising\\n\\n                      x)   Any other business\\n\\n\\n\
      \          7.9      Minutes of the meeting\\n\\n\\n          7.9.1    The Minutes of the meeting shall be\
      \ prepared as per the format provided at Form\\n                   No.: SF- 002 and sent to all members within\
      \ 2 working days preferably by mail/fax\\n                    followed by hardcopy. Safety Committee meeting\
      \ minutes shall also be displayed in\\n                    the notice board for wider publicity to all concerned.\\\
      n\\n\\n          7.10     Disciplinary Action\\n\\n\\n          7.10.1   The chairman shall inform the members\

      \ expenses\\n               and training fee towards the same shall be at the cost of the contractor.\\n\\\
      n\\n          10.0    SHE Inspection\\n\\n\\n          10.1     The contractor shall evolve and administer\
      \ a system of conducting SHE inspections\\n                 and other risk management analysis on a periodical\
      \ basis.\\n\\n\\n          10.2     The purpose of SHE inspection is to identify any variation in construction\
      \ activities and\\n                    operations, machineries, plant and equipment and processes against\
      \ the SHE Plan\\n                 and its supplementary procedures and programs.\\n\\n\\n          10.3  \
      \    Following SHE inspections program shall be adopted.\\n\\n                                 i)    Planned\
      \ General Inspection\\n\\n                                    ii)    Routine Inspection\\n\\n            \
      \                         iii)    Specific Inspection\\n\\n                          iv)   Other Inspection\\\
      n\\n\\n          10.3.1   Planned General Inspection\\n\\n\\n          10.3.1.1  Planned general inspections\
      \ are performed at predetermined intervals and  it usually\\n                    involves the representation\
      \ from both Contractor and the Employer.\\n\\n\\n          10.3.1.2  Inspections that will be classified under\
      \ this inspection program are:\\n\\n                                 i)    Monthly contractor and sub-contractors\
      \ site safety committee Inspection.\\n\\n                                    ii)    Weekly safety inspection\
      \ by construction supervisors (Contractors and Sub-\\n                            contractors).\\n\\n    \
      \                                 iii)    Daily safety inspection by contractor site SHE team.\\n\\n\\n  \
      \        10.3.2    Routine Inspection\\n\\n\\n          10.3.2.1  Routine inspections are often referring\
      \ to the inspection of work site, equipment and\\n                  temporary structures performed by site\
      \ and equipment operators and temporary\\n                     structure erectors.\\n\\n                 \
      \   Inspections that will be classified under this inspection program are:\\n\\n                         \
      \        i)     Daily Inspection of plant and equipment by operator\\n\\n                                \
      \    ii)    Weekly Inspection of scaffold by scaffolding supervisor\\n\\n                                \

    quote: "{\n  \"pdf_page\": 69,\n  \"text\": \"Pneumatic Tools                                          85\\\
      n          Scraper                                                 85\\n            Tractor              \
      \                                    84\\n\\n\\n         Noise emission limits apply to equipment used at\
      \ surface of the construction site during Night\\n                    time hours of 9 p.m. to 6 a.m.\\n\\\
      n      43.2.19     The adjustments for close in equipment noise measurement shall\\n                 be made\
      \ in accordance with Table-4.\\n\\n                                    TABLE – 4\\n              ADJUSTMENTS\
      \ FOR CLOSE-IN EQUIPMENT NOISE MEASUREMENTS\\n                    (Measurement Values to be subtracted from\
      \ Measured Sound)\\n         Distance (Feet)                      Level to Estimate Sound Level at 50 Feet\
      \ dB (A)\\n              19-21                                               8\\n              22-23     \
      \                                          7\\n              24-26                                       \
      \        6\\n              27-29                                               5\\n              30-33   \
      \                                            4\\n              34-37                                     \
      \          3\\n              38-42                                               2\\n              43-47 \
      \                                              1\\n              48-50                                   \
      \            0\\n\\n                                       TABLE- 5.\\n                          CONSTRUCTION\
      \ VIBRATION LIMITS\\n                             VIBRATION TYPE AND PERMISSIBL\\n       AGGREGATE DURATION\
      \            LIMIT\\n           Sustained (1 hr/day)                               0.01 in/sec (80 VdB re\
      \ 10-6 in/sec)\\n           Transient (<1 hr/day)                               0.03 in/sec (90 VdB re 10-6\
      \ in/sec)\\n           Transient (<10 min/day)                            0.10 in/sec (100 VdB re 10-6 in/sec)\\\
      n\\n\\n          43.2.20  When  Diesel Generator (DG) Sets  are used  for  operation  of equipment and\\n\
      \                   machinery, then ‘Standards and Guidelines  for  control  of Noise  Pollution from\\n \
      \                   Stationery DG Sets’, under Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 shall apply.\\n        \
      \ 43.2.21  Should the impact monitoring record noise levels which are:\\n                         indicative\
      \ of a deteriorating situation such that closer monitoring is reasonably\\n                            indicated,\
      \ or\\n                        when in the opinion of the Engineer additional measurements are required in\\\
      n                        view of deteriorating noise environment, then, the Engineer may require the\\n  \
      \                       Contractor to increase the frequency of impact monitoring at any one or more of\\\
      n                          the monitoring stations until the results indicate an improving and acceptable\\\
      n                             level of noise.\\n\\n        43.2..22    The Contractor  shall submit a copy\
      \  of monitoring  results. The  results should\\n                    represent  a statistical evaluation of\
      \ data for evaluation of trends and comparison\\n                      with noise emission standards.\\n\\\
      n        43.2.23   Where the Engineer determines that the recorded Noise level is significantly\\n       \
      \             greater than the acceptable levels, the Engineer may direct the Contractor to\\n           \
      \        take effective remedial measures including, but not limited to, reviewing noise\\n              \
      \    sources and modifying working procedures.\\n\\n         43.2.23    The Contractor shall inform the Engineer\
      \ of all steps taken to investigate cause of\\n                  exceedance and immediate action taken to\
      \ avoid further exceedance through\\n                       written reports and proposals for action under\
      \ an Event Contingency Plan.\\n\\n          43.3       Control Requirements\\n\\n\\n          43.3.1     Construction\
      \ material should be operated and transported in such a manner as not to\\n                     create unnecessary\
      \ noise as outlined below:\\n\\n\\n                                 i)    Perform Work within the procedures\
      \ outlined herein and comply with applicable\\n                        codes,  regulations, and  standards\
      \  established by  the  Central and  State\\n                     Government and their agencies.\"\n}"

      pending_manual_review\",\n  \"rotation\": 0,\n  \"text\": \"Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\\n  \
      \                                                        252\\n43.2.10  The Engineer shall monitor Contractor’s\
      \ performance of tasks specified, and  will\\n          inspect necessary records, reports and procedures\
      \ related to the control of noise.\\n\\n43.2.11  Impact monitoring shall be carried out at noise sensitive\
      \ receptor locations within 200\\n           feet of the construction site once each week and after a change\
      \ in construction\\n            activity. Construction noise measurements shall coincide with daytime and\
      \ nighttime\\n          periods of maximum noise generating construction activities.\\n\\n43.2.12  Noise Monitoring\
      \ data will be submitted in a Noise Measurement Report Form. It will\\n          contain the type of measurement,\
      \ duration of measurement, distance of monitoring\\n         from construction site, and construction equipment\
      \ working during monitoring period.\\n\\n43.2.13   appropriate  parameter  for measuring  construction  noise\
      \  impacts  shall be  the\\n          equivalent A-weighted sound pressure level (Leq) measured in decibels\
      \ (dB). The two\\n            statistical sound levels L10 and L90; the level exceeded for 10 and 90 percent\
      \ of the time\\n           respectively, shall also be recorded during monitoring. The L90 may be considered\
      \ as\\n          the ambient level into which the L10 as average peak level intrudes. The Lmax, Leq, L10\\\
      n        and L90 values will be reported in the noise measurement form along with allowable\\n         noise\
      \ limit. The duration of monitoring shall be for a minimum of 30 minutes.\\n\\n43.2..14  In no case  shall\
      \ the Contractor expose the public  to construction noise levels\\n         exceeding 90dBA (slow) or to impulsive\
      \ noise levels with a peak sound pressure level\\n         exceeding 140dB as measured on an impulse sound\
      \ level meter.\\n\\n43.2.15   Limit for construction noise is based on the existing ambient noise levels in\
      \ areas\\n          adjoining the construction sites.\\n\\n43.2.16 The noise levels emanating from any source\
      \ during construction, shall not exceed 5\\n         dB(A) or more above existing ambient pre-construction\
      \ noise levels when measured at\\n        a point outside the premises of the location of source. The same\
      \ may be varied from\\n         time to time by and at the sole discretion of the Engineer.\\n43.2.17  Where\
      \ there are no ambient noise measurements, the construction activities shall be\\n           limited to levels\
      \ measured at a distance of 200 feet from the construction limits or at\\n          the nearest affected building,\
      \ whichever is closer, as given in Table-2.\\n                                 TABLE-2\\n                \
      \  ALLOWABLE CONSTRUCTION NOISE\\n     LAND USE               MAXIMUM NOISE LEVELS- Lmax dB (A)\\n       \
      \                                     Day Time Night Time\\n          Residential                      75\
      \             65\\n          At all Times\\n          Commercial                                   85\\n \

      \ site during night time hours, the Contractor shall use\\n          only equipment that operating under full\
      \ load meets the noise limits specified in Table-\\n           3, if a sensitive receptor would be affected.\\\

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"47.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 73,\n      \"text\": \"\
      47.0 ENVIORNMENTAL MANAGEMENT\\n\\n             47.1 ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING\\n\\n              47.1.1 The\
      \  Contractor’s  Environmental  Team  shall  carry  out  the  monitoring  of\\n                     environmental\
      \ impacts during construction. Representative sensitive receivers in the\\n                           vicinity\
      \ of the works shall be monitored for noise and air quality impacts.\\n              47.1.2  For carrying\
      \ out impact monitoring for noise and air, equipment shall be provided,\\n                    operated and\
      \ maintained by the Contractor. The equipment shall be kept in a good\\n                       state  of \
      \ repair  in accordance  with  the  manufacturer’s recommendations and\\n                    maintained in\
      \ proper working order with sufficient spare equipment available in the\\n                     event of breakdown\
      \ to maintain the planned monitoring program.\\n              47.1.2 The calibration of monitoring instruments\
      \ and their respective calibrators shall be\\n                       carried out in accordance with the manufacturer’s\
      \ requirements to ensure they\\n                    perform to the same level of accuracy as stated in the\
      \ manufacturer’s specifications.\\n              47.1.3 Suspended Particulate Matter (SPM) levels shall be\
      \ measured by following the\\n                     standard high volume sampling method as set out in High\
      \ Volume Method for\\n                  Suspended Particulate, BIS: 5182-1981\\n              47.1.4  24-hour\
      \ average SPM concentration shall be measured by drawing air through a\\n                    High Volume Sampler\
      \ (HVS) fitted with pre-weighted Glass Fiber filter paper at an\\n                   average flow rate not\
      \ less than 1.1m3 per minute.\\n              47.1.5 The minimum requirements to the specifications of sound\
      \ level meter    should be\\n                   as given in IS: 9779-1981\\n              47.1.6  Engineer\
      \ will undertake baseline monitoring to establish background levels. Action\\n                      Level\
      \ of the Contractor shall be based on the results of baseline monitoring\\n                    program, which\
      \ will be made available to him prior to start of construction.\\n               47.1.7 The Contractor’s monitoring\
      \ program is summarized in Table –1.\\n\\n                                       TABLE-1\\n\\n           \
      \     SUMMARY OF CONTRACTOR’S MONITORING PROGRAMME\\n                Parameter                   Noise   \
      \                           Air\\n\\n          Sampling                Day Time (6.00 to 22.00 hrs):   RSPM,\
      \ SPM\\n                                             Lmax, Leq, L10, L90, L50            24-hours of the day\\\
      n                                        Night Time (9 PM – 6AM):      CO: 12 hrs from 8.00 to 20.00\\n  \
      \                                           Lmax, Leq, L10, L90, L50, Ldn          hrs.\\n\\n\\n         \
      \ Frequency               Once a week (when noise     Two 24-hour Samples every\\n           At each location\
      \              generating activities are           fifteen days at uniform intervals.\\n                 \

      n         Number of Locations        4 Locations                  2 Locations\\n           Duration  of  Monitoring\
      \ by  During Civil Construction        During Civil Construction\\n           Contractor\\n            Additional\
      \ Requirements     Adhoc monitoring as required.   Ad hoc monitoring as required\\n\\n\\n        47.2EVENT\
      \ CONTINGENCY PLAN\\n        The Contractor shall prepare an Event Contingency Plan under his Site Environmental\
      \ Plan. The\\n         purpose is to provide, in addition to monitoring activities, procedures for ensuring\
      \ that  if any\\n          environmental  exceedance  of  limiting  values  (either  accidental  or  through\
      \  inadequate\\n          implementation of mitigation measures on part of the Contractor) does occur, the\
      \ cause is\\n          quickly identified and remedied, and that the risk of a similar event recurring is\
      \ reduced.\\n\\n\\n          47.3      Air Quality\\n\\n\\n          47.3.1   The  Contractor  shall  take\
      \  all necessary  precautions  to minimise  fugitive  dust\\n                  emissions from operations involving\
      \ excavation, grading, and clearing of land and\\n                    disposal of waste. He shall not allow\
      \ emissions of fugitive dust from any transport,\\n                    handling, construction or storage activity\
      \ to remain visible in atmosphere beyond the\\n                    property line of emission source for any\
      \ prolonged period of time without notification to\\n                    the Employer.\"\n    },\n    {\n\
      \      \"pdf_page\": 74,\n      \"text\": \"47.3.2   The Contractor shall use construction equipment designed\
      \ and equipped to minimise\\n          or control air pollution. He shall maintain evidence of such design\
      \ and equipment and\\n       make these available for inspection by Employer.\\n\\n\\n47.3.3      If  after\
      \  commencement  of  construction  activity,  Employer  believes  that  the\\n          Contractor’s equipment\
      \ or methods of working are causing unacceptable air pollution\\n         impacts then these shall be inspected\
      \ and remedial proposals shall be drawn up by\\n          the Contractor, submitted for review to the Employer\
      \ and implemented.\\n\\n\\n47.3.4    In developing these remedial measures, the Contractor shall inspect and\
      \ review all\\n          dust sources that may be contributing to air pollution. Remedial measures include\
      \ use\\n           of additional / alternative equipment by the Contractor or maintenance / modification of\\\
      n           existing equipment of the Contractor.\\n\\n           In the event that approved remedial measures\
      \ are not being implemented and serious\\n         impacts persist, the Employer may direct the Contractor\
      \ to suspend work until the\\n        measures are implemented, as required under the Contract.\\n\\n\\n47.3.5\
      \    Contractor’s  transport  vehicles and  other equipment  shall conform  to emission\\n         standards\
      \  fixed by  Statutory  Agencies  of Government  of  India  or  the  State\\n        Government from time\
      \ to time. The Contractor shall carry out periodical checks and\\n         undertake remedial measures including\
      \ replacement,  if required, so as to operate\\n           within permissible norms.\\n\\n\\n47.3.6   The\
      \ Contractor shall establish and maintain records of routine maintenance program\\n            for internal\
      \ combustion engine powered vehicles and equipment used on this project.\\n       He shall keep records available\
      \ for inspection by Employer.\\n\\n\\n47.3.7   The Contractor shall cover loads of dust generating materials\
      \ like debris and soil being\\n          transported from construction  sites.  All trucks carrying loose\
      \ material should be\\n         covered and loaded with sufficient free- board to avoid spills through the\
      \ tailboard or\\n          sideboards.\\n\\n\\n47.3.8   The Contractor shall promptly transport all excavation\
      \ disposal materials of whatever\\n          kind so as not to delay work on the project. Stockpiling of materials\
      \  will only be\\n         allowed at sites designated by the Employer. The Contractor shall place excavation\\\
      n          materials in the dumping/disposal areas designated in the plans as given in the\\n           specifications.\\\
      n\\n\\n47.3.9   The temporary dumping areas shall be maintained by the Contractor at all times until\\n  \
      \        the excavate is re-utilised for backfilling or as directed by Employer. Dust control\\n         \
      \   activities shall continue even during any work stoppage.\\n\\n\\n\\n\\n47.3.10  The Contractor shall place\
      \ material in a manner that will minimize dust production.\\n          Material shall be minimized each day\
      \ and wetted, to minimize dust production. During\\n          dry weather, dust control methods must be used\
      \ daily especially on windy, dry days to\\n         prevent any dust from blowing across the site perimeter.\\\
      n\\n\\n47.3.11  The Contractor shall water down construction sites as required to suppress dust,\\n      \
      \    during handling of excavation soil or debris or during demolition. The Contractor will\\n       make\
      \ water sprinklers, water supply and water delivering equipment available at any\\n         time that it is\
      \ required for dust control use. Dust screens will be used, as feasible when\\n           additional dust\
      \  control measures are needed  specially where the work  is near\\n          sensitive receptors.\\n\\n\\\
      n47.3.12  The Contractor shall provide a wash pit or a wheel washing and/or vehicle cleaning\\n          \
      \   facility at the exits from work sites such as construction depots and batching plants. At\\n         such\
      \ facility, high-pressure water jets will be directed at the wheels of vehicles to\\n        remove all spoil\
      \ and dirt.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 75,\n      \"text\": \"47.3.13  The Contractor shall design\
      \ and implement his blasting techniques so as to minimise\\n                     dust, noise, vibration generation\
      \ and prevention fly rock.\\n\\n\\n          47.3.14   Blasting technique should be consistent not only with\
      \ nature and quaintly of rock to be\\n                    blasted but also the location of blasting.\\n\\\
      n          47.3.15  The  contractor  shall  give  preference  to  explosives  with  better  environmental\\\
      n                      characteristics.\\n\\n          47.3.16  The Contractor shall protect structures, utilities,\
      \ pavements roads and other facilities\\n                  from disfiguration and damage as a result of his\
      \ activities. Where this is not possible,\\n                    the contractor  shall restore the structures,\
      \  utilities, pavements, roads and other\\n                          facilities to their original or better,\
      \ failing which the rectification/restoration work shall\\n                be carried out at the risk and\
      \ cost of the contractor.\\n\\n\\n          47.3.17  The Contractor shall submit to the Employer an Air Monitoring\
      \ and Control Plan\\n               (AMCP) under contract specific Site Environmental Plan to guide construction\
      \ activity\\n                     insofar as it relates to monitoring, controlling and mitigating air pollution.\\\
      n\\n\\n          47.4    AIR MONITORING\\n          47.4.1    Construction activities that will generate dust\
      \ impacts include excavation (including\\n                     related activities), material handling and\
      \ stockpiling, vehicular movement, and wind\\n                   erosion of unpaved work areas.\\n\\n    \
      \      47.4.2 The impact of fugitive dust on ambient air pollution depends on the quantity generated, as\\\
      n                     well as the drift potential of the dust particles injected into the atmosphere. Large\
      \ dust\\n                      particles will settle out near the source and smaller particles are likely\
      \ to undergo\\n                    dispersal over greater distance from the sources and impeded settling.\
      \ SPM levels will\\n                be monitored to evaluate the dust impact during the construction phase\
      \ of the Project.\\n\\n          47.4.3   The  Air  Quality  Monitoring and  Control Plan (AMCP)  in  contract-specific\
      \  Site\\n                   Environmental Plan prepared by the Contractor shall establish procedures to monitor\\\
      n                  impact air quality and measures to control air pollution including dust suppression due\\\
      n                      to construction activities at work sites. This plan shall contain description of activities\\\
      n                      that  will cause degradation  in  air  quality, environmental procedures  to manage\\\
      n                     pollutants to minimise the  air  pollution, monitoring program, record keeping and\\\
      n                      reporting.\\n\\n          47.4.4   The Engineer shall monitor Contractor’s performance\
      \ of tasks specified, and will inspect\\n                  necessary records, reports and procedures related\
      \ to the control of air quality given in\\n               AMCP.\\n          47.4.5    Information gathered\
      \ during the AMCP  will be catalogued and maintained by the\\n                    Contractor and shall be\
      \ available for review by the Engineer.\\n\\n          47.4.6   The exact location of the air monitoring stations\
      \ located near air sensitive receptors\\n                    adjoining the construction sites, such as residences,\
      \ schools, hotels and hospitals and\\n                  placement of monitoring equipment thereat shall be\
      \ agreed with the Engineer prior to\\n               commencement of air monitoring program.\\n\\n       \
      \   47.4.7   Impact monitoring during the course  of the Works  shall be carried out  at the\\n          \
      \          monitoring stations for two days (continuous twenty-four hours) every fifteen days and\\n     \
      \            where there is a perceived air quality problem.\\n          47.4.8   The Contractor shall construct\
      \ suitable fence, lockable gate, 220V AC power point and\\n                     suitable access at each air\
      \ monitoring station.  Monitoring stations shall be free from\\n                      local obstructions or\
      \ sheltering.\\n\\n\\n          47.4.9   Should impact monitoring record dust levels which are:\\n\\n\\n \
      \                      indicative of a deteriorating situation such that closer monitoring is reasonably\\\
      n                          indicated, or\\n\\n\\n                      when in the opinion of the Engineer\
      \ additional measurements are required in view\\n                          of deteriorating air quality,\"\
      \n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 76,\n      \"text\": \"Then the Engineer may require the Contractor to\
      \ increase the frequency of impact\\n          monitoring at any one or more of the monitoring stations until\
      \ the results indicate an\\n         improving and acceptable level of air quality.\\n\\n\\n47.4.10  The Contractor\
      \ shall keep records of air quality monitoring (including location, date,\\n           time). The Contractor\
      \ shall submit a copy of monitoring results to the Engineer. The\\n           results should represent a \
      \ statistical evaluation of data by calculating maximum,\\n        minimum, mean, standard deviation, geometric\
      \ mean and percentile calculations for\\n          evaluation of frequency distribution, trends, and comparison\
      \ with emission standards.\\n\\n\\n47.4.11  The National Ambient Air Quality Standards given in Air (Prevention\
      \ and Control of\\n           Pollution) Act, 1981 may be referred by the Contractor for Limit Levels of SPM\
      \ in\\n         ambient  air which may be followed  in estimating the  pollution  level caused by\\n     \
      \     Contractor’s activities.\\n\\n47.4.12  Where  the  Engineer  determines  that  the  recorded  dust \
      \ (TSP)  level  is\\n          significantly  greater  than  the  Limit  levels,  the Engineer may  direct\
      \  the\\n         Contractor to take effective remedial measures including, but not limited to,\\n       \
      \  reviewing dust sources and modifying working procedures.\\n\\n47.4.13  Where the recorded baseline levels\
      \ exceed the ambient air quality standards, then at\\n         such locations the action level is the recorded\
      \ base line. Contractor shall take all\\n           effective remedial measures to contain the levels to their\
      \ baseline value as a result of\\n           his activities. The action level may be varied by and at the\
      \ sole discretion of the\\n         Engineer.\\n\\n47.4.14 The Contractor shall inform the Engineer of  all\
      \ steps taken to investigate cause of\\n        exceedance and immediate action taken to avoid further exceedance\
      \ through written\\n         reports and proposals for action under an Event Contingency Plan.\"\n    }\n\

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"48.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 76,\n      \"text\": \"\
      48.0     Water Quality\\n\\n\\n48.1    The Contractor shall comply with the Indian Government legislation\
      \ and other State\\n          regulations in existence in Delhi insofar as they relate to water pollution\
      \ control and\\n          monitoring. A drainage system should be constructed at the commencement of the\\\
      n         Works, to drain off all surface water from the work site into suitable drain outlet.\\n\\n\\n48.2\
      \    The Contractor shall provide adequate precautions to ensure that no spoil or debris of\\n        any\
      \ kind is pushed, washed, falls or deposited on land adjacent to the site perimeter\\n          including\
      \ public roads or existing stream courses and drains within or adjacent to the\\n            site. In the\
      \ event of any spoil or debris from construction works being deposited or any\\n               silt washed\
      \ down to any area, then all such spoil, debris or material and silt shall be\\n         immediately removed\
      \ and the affected land and areas restored to their natural state by\\n          the Contractor to the satisfaction\
      \ of the Employer.\\n\\n\\n48.3    Due to lowering of potable water supplies in Bangalore and subsequent contamination\\\
      n           of ground water, the Contractor is not allowed to discharge water from the site without\\n   \
      \       the approval of the Employer. The Contractor must comply with the requirements of\\n          the\
      \ Local Ground Water Board for discharge of water arising from dewatering. Any\\n         water obtained from\
      \ dewatering systems installed in the works must be either re-used\\n            for construction purposes\
      \ and this water may subsequently be discharged to the\\n         drainage system or,  if not re-used, recharged\
      \ to the ground water at suitable aquifer\\n           levels. The Contractor must submit his proposals for\
      \ approval of Employer, on his\\n         proposed locations of dewatering of excavation and collection of\
      \ water for either\\n          construction re-use  or recharge  directly  to  aquifers. The  Contractor’s\
      \ recharge\\n         proposals must be sufficient for recharging of the quantity of water remaining after\\\
      n         deduction of water re-used for construction. During dewatering, the contractor shall\\n        \
      \ monitor ground water levels from wells to ensure that draw down levels do not exceed\\n          allowable\
      \ limits.  The Contractor will not be permitted to directly discharge, to the\\n         drainage system,\
      \ unused ground  water  obtaining  from  the  excavation  without\\n          obtaining approval of Employer\
      \ or the Agency controlling the system.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 77,\n      \"text\": \"48.4\
      \    The Contractor shall ensure that earth, bentonite, chemicals and concrete agitator\\n               \
      \   washings etc. are not deposited in the watercourses but are suitably collected and\\n                \
      \   residue disposed off in a manner approved by local authorities.\\n\\n\\n          48.5       All water\
      \ and waste products (surface runoff and wastewater) arising on the site shall\\n                be  collected\
      \ and removed from  the  site  via a  suitable and properly designed\\n                  temporary drainage\
      \ system and disposed off at a location and in a manner that will\\n                 cause neither pollution\
      \ nor nuisance.\\n\\n\\n          48.6    Any mud slurry from drilling, tunnelling, diaphragm wall construction\
      \ or grouting etc.\\n                      shall not be discharged into the drainage system unless treatment\
      \ is carried out that\\n                          will remove silt, mud particles, bentonite etc. The Contractor\
      \ shall provide treatment\\n                          facilities as necessary to prevent the discharge of\
      \ contaminated ground water.\\n\\n\\n          48.7    The Contractor shall discharge wastewater arising out\
      \ of site office, canteen or toilet\\n                          facilities constructed by him into sewers\
      \ after obtaining prior approval of agency\\n                      controlling the system.  A wastewater drainage\
      \ system shall be provided to drain\\n                  wastewater into the sewerage system.\\n\\n\\n    \
      \      48.8    The bentonite mixing, treatment and handling system shall be established by the\\n        \
      \             contractor giving due regard to its environmental impacts. The disposal of redundant\\n    \
      \                bentonite shall be carefully considered whether in bulk or liquid form. The disposal\\n \
      \                    location will be advised and agreed with the relevant authorities.\\n\\n\\n         \
      \ 48.9    The Contractor shall take measures to prevent discharge of oil and grease during\\n            \
      \         spillage from reaching drainage system or any water body. Oil removal / interceptors\\n        \
      \              shall be provided to treat oil waste from workshop areas etc.\\n\\n         48.10   The Contractor\
      \ shall apply to the appropriate authority for installing bore wells for\\n                   water supply\
      \ at site.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\": \"48.0     Water Quality\",\n  \"retained_lines\": [\n    {\n\

    quote: "{\n  \"extraction_method\": \"geometric_sort\",\n  \"has_extracted_text\": true,\n  \"page_rect\": [\n\
      \    0.0,\n    0.0,\n    595.219970703125,\n    842.0\n  ],\n  \"pdf_page\": 80,\n  \"review_status\": \"\
      pending_manual_review\",\n  \"rotation\": 0,\n  \"text\": \"Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\\n  \
      \                                                          264\\n                      PART - V: PENALTY AND\
      \ AWARDS\\n\\n\\n   56.0     Charges to be recovered from contractor for unsafe act or condition\\n\\n\\n\
      \   56.1    BMRC has built an image of safety conscious organisation meticulously over a period\\n       \
      \       of seven years. Any reportable accident (fatality / injury) results in loss of life and/or\\n    \
      \         property damage. These accidents not only result in loss of life but also damage the\\n        \
      \     reputation of BMRC. Most of the accidents are avoidable and caused preliminary due\\n              to\
      \ contractors’ negligence. Hence BMRC shall recover the cost of damages from the\\n             contractors\
      \ for every reportable incident (fatality / injury).\\n\\n\\n   56.2      In addition every BMRC work  site\
      \  is exposed to public scrutiny as the work  is\\n            executed just on the right-of-way. Any unsafe\
      \ act  / unsafe condition observed by\\n              public further damages our reputation. Because of the\
      \ non-voluntary compliance of\\n             contractors to the condition of contract on SHE and project SHE\
      \ manual, BMRC has\\n           been forced to establish safety-enforcing organisation. The cost of established\
      \ such\\n             organisation is to be recovered from contractors for all observed safety violations\

      \ to be recovered from contractor for unsafe act or condition \\n \\n56.1  \\nBMRC has built an image of safety\

      \ injury) results in loss of life and/or \\nproperty damage. These accidents not only result in loss of life\
      \ but also damage the \\nreputation of BMRC. Most of the accidents are avoidable and caused preliminary due\
      \ \\nto contractors’ negligence. Hence BMRC shall recover the cost of damages from the \\ncontractors for\
      \ every reportable incident (fatality / injury). \\n \\n56.2  \\nIn addition every BMRC work site is exposed\
      \ to public scrutiny as the work is \\nexecuted just on the right-of-way. Any unsafe act / unsafe condition\
      \ observed by \\npublic further damages our reputation. Because of the non-voluntary compliance of \\ncontractors\
      \ to the condition of contract on SHE and project SHE manual, BMRC has \\nbeen forced to establish safety-enforcing\
      \ organisation. The cost of established such \\norganisation is to be recovered from contractors for all observed\
      \ safety violations at \\nsites. \\n \\n56.3  \\nThe following table indicates the Safety, Health and Environment\

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"18.0\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 20,\n      \"text\": \"\
      18.0     TENDER OPENING\\n\\n         18.1     The tenders shall be opened online in the eProcurement Portal\
      \ by the Employer on the\\n                  scheduled date and time of tender opening as mentioned in NIT\
      \ or as per subsequent\\n                amendment if any at the office of the General Manager (Contracts)\
      \ address mentioned in NIT.\\n                               (If such scheduled date for opening of Bid is\
      \ subsequently declared as a Public Holiday by\\n                    the Employer, the next official working\
      \ day shall be deemed to be the date of opening of the\\n                      Bids).\\n\\n         18.2 \
      \    On opening the technical bid, the tender opening committee will first check the tender security\\n  \
      \              (EMD) documents submitted by the bidder on the eProcurement Portal.\\n\\n         18.4    \
      \  Tender  submittals/ documents  of  all  online  bids accepted by the Employer on the\\n               \
      \   eProcurement Portal shall be downloaded for further technical evaluation.\\n\\n         18.5     The Financial\
      \ Bid(s) will be opened on the eProcurement portal on a subsequent date after\\n                    the evaluation\
      \ of technical bids. Financial Bids of only those tenderers whose submissions\\n                   are found\
      \ substantially responsive and technically compliant as per clause 22.1 of ITT will be\\n                \
      \  opened. The time of opening of financial bids shall be informed through the eProcurement\\n           \
      \            Portal. Bidders shall visit the eProcurement Portal regularly for updates.\"\n    }\n  ],\n \
      \ \"heading_line\": \"18.0     TENDER OPENING\",\n  \"review_status\": \"pending_manual_review\"\n}"

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"14\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 133,\n      \"text\": \"\
      14         Risk and Responsibility\\n\\nIndemnity        14.1      The Contractor shall indemnify and hold\
      \ harmless the Employer, the Engineer, the\\n                            Designated Contractors, representatives\
      \ and employees from and against  all\\n                                 actions, suits, proceedings, claims,\
      \ damages, losses, expenses and demands of\\n                             every nature and description, by\
      \ reasons of any act or omissions of the Contractor,\\n                                  his representative\
      \ or his employees in the execution of the Works, including\\n                                professional\
      \ services provided by the Contractor or in the guarding the same.\\n                         These indemnification\
      \ obligations shall include but not be limited to claims,\\n                          damages,  losses, damage\
      \ proceedings, charges and expenses which are\\n                                   attributable to:\\n\\n\
      \                                    (a)   sickness, or disease, or death of, or injury to any person; and\\\
      n                                    (b)   loss of, or damage to, or destruction of any property (other than\
      \ the Works)\\n                                       including consequential loss of use; and\\n        \
      \                             (c)   Loss, damage or costs arising from the carriage of Plant and Materials\\\
      n                                     and/or ownership or chartering of marine vessels by the Contractor,\
      \ or any\\n                                      sub-contractor of any tier.\\n\\n                       \
      \  The Contractor shall also indemnify and save harmless the Employer from and\\n                        \
      \       against all claims and proceedings on account of infringements of patents rights,\\n             \
      \                  design, trademark name etc. as detailed out in Sub Clause 5.8.\\n\\n                  \
      \                    All sums payable by way of compensation under these conditions shall be\\n          \
      \                   considered reasonable compensation payable to the Employer, without reference\\n     \
      \                             to the actual loss or damage sustained, and whether or not any damage shall\
      \ have\\n                          been sustained. The decision of the Engineer as to compensation claimed\
      \ shall\\n                          be final and binding.\\n\\nContractor’s      14.2      The Contractor\
      \ shall take full responsibility for the care of the Works, or any part\\nCare of the                    \
      \ thereof, including full responsibility for the care of any work being manufactured,\\nWorks            \
      \             or stored off-Site for inclusion in the Works, or in the course of transportation to\\n    \
      \                           the Site, and for the care of Contractor’s Equipment, Temporary Works, Plant and\\\
      n                          any other Material, whatsoever, on the Site or delivered to or placed on the Site\
      \ in\\n                             connection with, or for the purpose of the Works.\\n\\n              \
      \           The Contractor shall take this responsibility from the Commencement Date until\\n            \
      \                   the date of issue of the Taking Over Certificate, when responsibility shall pass to\\\
      n                               the Employer. If the Engineer issues a Taking Over Certificate for any Section\
      \ or\\n                                 part of the Works, the Contractor shall cease to be responsible for\
      \ the care of that\\n                              Section or part from the date of issue of such Taking Over\
      \ Certificate when\\n                                  responsibility shall pass to the Employer.\\n\\n  \
      \                       The Contractor shall take responsibility for the care of any outstanding work which\\\
      n                                        is required to be completed prior to the expiry of the Contract Period,\
      \ until the\\n                            Engineer confirms in writing that such outstanding work has been\
      \ completed.\\n                                                   If any loss or damage happens to the Works,\
      \ any other property or person, arising\\n                            from any cause other than the Employer's\
      \ risks listed in Sub-Clause14.3, during\\n                               the period for which the Contractor\
      \ is responsible, the Contractor shall rectify such\\n                                loss or damage, at his\
      \ cost, so that the Works conform with the Contract or at the\\n                               option of the\
      \ Employer, will pay or allow to the Employer the cost of rectifying such\\n                             \
      \   loss or damage. Notwithstanding such loss or damage, the Contractor shall\\n                         \
      \   proceed with the execution of Works in  all respects in accordance with the\\n                       \
      \       Contract and the Engineer's instructions. The Contractor shall also be liable for\\n             \
      \             any loss or damage to the Works caused by any operations carried out by the\\n             \
      \                  Contractor after the date of issue of the Taking Over Certificate.\\n\\nEmployer’s    \
      \   14.3      The Employer's risks of loss or damage to physical property in India and of death\\nRisks  \
      \                   and personal injury occurring in India in consequence of the performance of\\n       \
      \                          obligations under the Contract are:\\n\\n                                    (a)\
      \   War, hostilities (whether war be declared or not), invasion, act of foreign\\n                       \
      \           enemies, act of terrorism.\\n                                    (b)    rebellion, revolution,\
      \ insurrection, or military or usurped power, or civil war,\\n                                         within\
      \ India,\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 134,\n      \"text\": \"(c)     riot, commotion or disorder\
      \ by persons unless solely restricted to or caused\\n                                     by employees of\
      \ Contractor or of sub-contractors currently or formerly\\n                                   engaged in the\
      \ Works,\\n                                          (d)   Ionising radiations, or contamination by radio-activity\
      \ from any nuclear fuel,\\n                                            or from any nuclear waste from the\
      \ combustion of nuclear fuel, radio-active\\n                                                toxic explosive,\
      \ or other hazardous properties of any explosive nuclear\\n                                     assembly or\
      \ nuclear component of such an assembly, except to the extent\\n                                         \
      \      to which the Contractor may be responsible for the use of any radio-active\\n                     \
      \                         material, Pressure waves caused by  aircraft or other  aerial devices\\n       \
      \                                   (e)    travelling at sonic or supersonic speeds, and\\n              \
      \                       use or occupation by the Employer of any part of the Works, except as\\n         \
      \                                             (f)   may be specified in the Contract.\\n\\n    Consequences\
      \   14.4             If an Employer’s risk results in loss or damage, the Contractor shall promptly notify\\\
      n     of Employer’s                the Engineer and shall rectify this loss or damage to the extent required\
      \ by the\\n    Risks                        Engineer.\\n\\n                                              \
      \              If the Contractor suffers delay and/or incurs cost from rectifying this loss or\\n        \
      \                      damage, the Contractor shall give notice to the Engineer and shall be entitled to\\\
      n                                      claim:\\n\\n                                          (a)   Extension\
      \ of time for any such delay,  if completion is or will be delayed,\\n                                   \
      \    under Sub-Clause 8.4, and\\n                                          (b)   Amount of such cost, which\
      \ shall be added to the Contract Price.\\n\\n     Contractor’s      14.5      The Contractor's risks are all\

      n                                Employer to rescind the Contract.\\n\\n                                 \
      \     Failure or delay by the Employer or the Engineer, to hand over to the Contractor\\n                \
