      \ plant\\n                                      or machinery, which under the Contract, is the responsibility\
      \ of the Employer, shall\\n                                           in no way affect or vitiate the Contract\
      \ or alter the character thereof, or entitle the\\n                                    Contractor to damages\
      \ or compensation thereof and in any such case, the\\n                                 Engineer shall extend\
      \ the time period for the completion of the Contract, as in his\\n                                    opinion\

      n                                            e.  Any act of prevention or Breach of the Contract by the Employer\

      \                                      f.  Any order of Court restraining the performance of the Contract\
      \ in full or in\\n                                     any part thereof and the Contractor not being in default\
      \ as to reason of\\n                                      such order of court.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"\
      pdf_page\": 105,\n      \"text\": \"g.  Any other event or occurrence which, according to the Employer is\
      \ not\\n                                due to the Contractor’s failure or fault, and is beyond his control\
      \ without\\n                                  Employer being responsible for the same.\\n                \

    quote: "{\n  \"clause_id\": \"17\",\n  \"fragments\": [\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 139,\n      \"text\": \"\
      17         Claims, Disputes and Conciliation\\n                         Any and all Disputes shall be settled\
      \ in accordance with the provision of this\\n                           Clause\\nProcedure for     17.1  \
      \           If the Contractor intends to claim any additional payment under any clause of\\nClaims       \
      \               these Conditions or otherwise, the Contractor shall give notice to the Engineer as\\n    \
      \                      soon as possible and in any event within 28 days of the start of the event giving\\\
      n                                   rise to the claim.\\n\\n                         The Contractor shall\
      \ keep such contemporary records as may be necessary to\\n                                substantiate any\
      \ claim, either on the Site or at any other location acceptable to the\\n                              Engineer.\
      \ Without admitting the Employer’s liability, the Engineer shall, on receipt\\n                          \
      \        of such notice, inspect such records and may instruct the Contractor to keep\\n                 \
      \                 further contemporary records. The Contractor shall permit the Engineer to inspect\\n   \
      \                                        all such records, and shall (if instructed) submit copies to the\
      \ Engineer.\\n\\n\\n                               Within 28 days of such notice, or such other time as may\
      \ be agreed by the\\n                              Engineer, the Contractor shall send to the Engineer a fully\
      \ detailed claim which\\n                               includes full supporting particulars of the basis\
      \ of the claim and additional payment\\n                               claimed. If the event or circumstance\
      \ giving rise to the claim has a continuing\\n                                    effect:\\n\\n          \
      \                        a.  the initial fully detailed claim shall be considered as interim;\\n\\n      \
      \                            b.  the Contractor shall send further interim claims at monthly intervals, giving\
      \ the\\n                                  cumulative amount claimed, and any such further particulars as the\
      \ Engineer\\n                         may reasonably require; and\\n\\n                                  \
      \  c.  the contractor shall send a final claim within 28 days after the end of effects\\n                \
      \                      resulting from the event or circumstance, or within such other period as may\\n   \
      \                          be proposed by the Contractor and approved by the Engineer.\\n\\n             \
      \                                      If the Contractor fails to comply with this Sub-clause, he shall not\
      \ be entitled to\\n                               claim any additional payment.\\n\\nPayment for      17.2\
      \      The Contractor  shall be  entitled  to have included  in any Interim Payment\\nClaims             \
      \              Certificate such amount for any claim as the Engineer considers due, after taking\\n      \
      \                        approval from  the Employer.  If the  particulars supplied are  insufficient  to\\\
      n                                substantiate the whole of the claim, the Contractor shall be entitled to\
      \ payment for\\n                           such part of the claim as has been substantiated.\\n\\nNo Legal\
      \         17.3      Any and all Disputes shall be settled in accordance with the provisions of Clause\\naction\
      \ till                     17. No action at law concerning or arising out of any Dispute shall be commenced\\\
      nDispute                      unless and until all applicable Dispute resolution procedures set out in Clause\
      \ 17\\nSettlement                      shall have been finally exhausted in relation to that Dispute or any\
      \ Dispute out of\\nProcedure is                which that Dispute shall have arisen with which  it may be\
      \ or may have been\\nExhausted                   connected.\\n\\nNotice of         17.4     A Dispute shall\
      \ be deemed to arise when one party serves a notice in writing\\nDispute                         (hereinafter\
      \ called a \\\"Notice of Dispute\\\") within 30 days from the date of rejection\\n                       \
      \           of claim by the parties.\\n\\n\\nDispute           17.5       Disputes shall be settled through\
      \ Conciliation procedures as established by “The\\nResolution                      Arbitration and Conciliation\
      \ Act, 1996” and as amended from time to time.\\n\\nConciliation      17.6        Within 60 days of receipt\
      \ of Notice of Dispute, either party shall refer the matter in\\n                               dispute to\
      \ conciliation. Conciliation proceedings shall be initiated within 30 days\\n                            \
      \      of one party  inviting the other  in  writing  to  Conciliation.  Conciliation  shall\\n          \
      \             commence when the other party accepts in writing this invitation.  If the invitation\\n    \
      \                                    is not accepted, then Conciliation shall not take place.    If the party\
      \ initiating\\n                                   conciliation does not receive a reply within 30 days from\
      \ the date on which he\\n                           sends the invitation, he may elect to treat this as a\
      \ rejection of the invitation to\\n                                  conciliate and inform the other party\
      \ accordingly.\\n                         The Conciliation shall be undertaken by one Conciliator selected\
      \ from a panel of\\n                                 Conciliators maintained by the Employer. The Conciliator\
      \ shall assist the parties\\n                                  to reach an amicable settlement in an independent\
      \ and impartial manner.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 140,\n      \"text\": \"Conciliation      17.7\
      \      The Employer shall maintain a panel of Conciliators with requisite qualifications\\n    Procedure \
      \                and professional experience who shall be from serving or retired engineers of\\n        \
      \                      Government Departments, or of Public Sector Undertakings. Panel  list not to\\n   \
      \                                  include serving or former employees of the Employer. Out of this panel,\
      \ a list of\\n                                    three Conciliators shall be sent to the Contractor who shall\
      \ choose one of them to\\n                                     act as Conciliator and conduct conciliation\
      \ proceedings in accordance with “The\\n                                        Arbitration and Conciliation\
      \ Act, 1996”, of India. The party serving notice of dispute\\n                              on the other party\
      \ shall also serve such notice on the Conciliator chosen as per\\n                                       \
      \    this Clause. The Employer at the time of offering the panel of Conciliators to be\\n                \
      \                  appointed as Conciliator shall also supply the information with regard to the\\n      \
      \                                  qualifications of the said Conciliators nominated in the panel along with\
      \ their\\n                                     professional experience, phone nos. and addresses to the Contractor.\\\
      n\\n                                        In the event of the Contractor not choosing the Conciliator from\
      \ the panel furnished\\n                               by the Employer, within a period of 30 days, the Employer\
      \ is at liberty to choose\\n                              and nominate a Conciliator from the same panel and\
      \ communicate to the\\n                                    Contractor which will be final and binding on the\
      \ Contractor.\\n\\n\\n                             The Employer and the Contractor  shall  in good  faith\
      \ co-operate  with the\\n                                       Conciliator and, in particular, shall endeavour\
      \ to comply with requests by the\\n                                       Conciliator to submit written materials,\
      \ provide evidence and attend meetings.\\n                             Each party may, on his own initiative\
      \ or at the invitation of the Conciliator, submit\\n                                        to the Conciliator\
      \ suggestions for the settlement of the dispute.\\n\\n\\n                         When it appears to the Conciliator\
      \ that there exist elements of a settlement which\\n                          may be acceptable to the parties,\
      \ he shall formulate the terms of a possible\\n                                    settlement and submit them\
      \ to the parties for their observations. After receiving\\n                                    the observations\
      \ of the parties, the Conciliator may reformulate the terms of a\\n                                    possible\
      \ settlement in the light of such observations.\\n\\n\\n                                                 \
      \           If the Parties reach agreement on a settlement of the dispute, they may draw up\\n           \
      \                   and sign a  written settlement agreement.  If requested by the Parties, the\\n       \
      \                                Conciliator may draw up, or assist the Parties in drawing up, the settlement\\\
      n                                 agreement.\\n                         When the Parties sign the settlement\
      \ agreement, it shall be final and binding on\\n                                    the parties and persons\
      \ claiming under them respectively.\\n                             The Conciliator shall authenticate the\
      \ settlement agreement and furnish a copy\\n                                     thereof to each of the Parties.\\\
      n\\n\\n                            To the fullest extent feasible, the conciliatory process must be concluded\
      \ within a\\n\\n                                    period of sixty days subsequent to the acknowledgment\
      \ of the appointment notice\\n\\n                               by the Conciliator.\\n\\n                \
      \             The Parties shall not initiate, during the conciliation proceedings, any judicial\\n       \
      \                           proceedings in respect of a dispute that is the subject matter of the conciliation\\\
      n                                   proceedings.\\n\\n    Termination of    17.8      The conciliation proceedings\
      \ shall be terminated:\\n     Conciliation                    a.  by the signing of the settlement agreement\
      \ by the Parties on the date of\\n    Proceedings                    agreement; or\\n                    \
      \                    b.  by written declaration of the Conciliator, after consultation with the Parties, to\\\
      n                                        the effect further efforts at conciliation are no longer justified,\
      \ on the date of\\n                                           declaration; or\\n                         \
      \                 c.  by a written declaration of the Parties to the Conciliator to the effect that the\\\
      n                                             conciliation proceedings are terminated, on the date of declaration;\
      \ or\\n                                        d.  by a written declaration of a Party to the other Party\
      \ and the Conciliator,  if\\n                                       appointed, to the effect that the conciliation\
      \ proceedings are terminated, on\\n                                        the date of declaration.\\n   \
      \                         Upon termination of the conciliation proceedings, the Conciliator shall fix the\
      \ costs\\n                                        of the conciliation and give written notice thereof to the\
      \ Parties. The costs shall be\\n                                borne equally by the Parties unless settlement\
      \ agreement provides for a different\\n                                   apportionment. All other expenses\
      \ incurred by a Party shall be borne by that Party.\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"pdf_page\": 141,\n      \"text\"\
      : \"Suspension of   17.9       The reference to Conciliation shall proceed not withstanding that the Works\
      \ shall\\nWork on                      not then be or be alleged to be complete, provided always that the\
      \ obligations of\\nAccount of                    the Employer, Engineer and the Contractor shall not be altered\
      \ by reasons of\\nconciliation                     conciliation being conducted during the progress of the\
      \ Works. Neither party shall\\n                          be entitled to suspend the work or part of the work\
      \ to which the dispute relates on\\n                            account of conciliation and payments to the\
      \ Contractor shall continue to be made\\n                                     in terms of the Contract.\\\
      n\\nJudicial          17.10        In the event that a dispute remains unresolved via the conciliation process,\
      \ the\\nRecourses                   aggrieved party may seek judicial recourses.\\n\\nJurisdiction      17.11\
      \      Any suit or application, arising out of any dispute or differences on account of this\\nof Courts \
      \                     contract shall be filed in a competent court at Bangalore, Karnataka only and no\\n\
      \                               other court or any other district of the country shall have any jurisdiction\
      \ on the\\n                                matter.\\n\\nMatters finally    17.12            If the Contractor\
      \ (s) does/do not prefer his/ their specific and final claims in writing,\\ndetermined by                \
      \ within a period of 90 days of receiving the intimation from the Employer that the\\nthe Employer       \
      \               final bill is ready for payment, he/they will be deemed to have waived his/their\\n      \
      \                        claims (s) and the Employer shall be discharged and released of all liabilities under\\\
      n                               the contract in respect of these claims.\"\n    }\n  ],\n  \"heading_line\"\
      : \"17         Claims, Disputes and Conciliation\",\n  \"review_status\": \"pending_manual_review\",\n  \"\
      title\": \"Claims, Disputes and Conciliation\"\n}"

“fraudulent practice” means a misrepresentation\n                      of facts in order to influence an evaluation process or the execution of a contract, and\n                    includes misleading or false representation in forms or statements or attachment\n                   submitted and collusive practices among Bidders (prior to or after bid submission)\n                  designed to establish bid prices at artificial, non-competitive levels and to deprive the\n                 Employer of the benefits of free and open competitions;\n\n                  (g) have been considered ineligible due to execution of Bid–Securing Declaration by any\n                    Central Govt./State Govt./PSUs;\n\n                  (h) have been Black  listed/debarred /banned business by any Central Govt./State\n                 Govt./PSUs or Local Authority or World Bank or ADB or JICA or any other International\n                   Financing Institution, or any entity controlled by them;\n\n                         (i) have left/abandoned the awarded works on his own in the last 05 years;"

If audited Balance sheet of any year other than the last financial \nyear ending with 2025-2026 is not submitted even when requested for as a clarification under clause 20 of ITT, then the Tender will be \nconsidered as non-responsive. \n5) \nAll documents shall reflect the stand-alone financial status of the Tenderer and not the Tenderer’s parent companies, subsidiaries, or \naffiliates. \n6) \nFor the purpose of evaluation, amounts in foreign currencies shall be converted to equivalent INR as per the following procedure: \nIn cases where the financial data is denominated in a currency other than Indian Rupees, it shall be converted into the equivalent value \nin Indian Rupees by adopting the exchange rate between the foreign currency and INR prevailing on the last day of the respective \nfinancial year, as published on the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) website, for the purpose of bid evaluation. \n7) \nTo align a January–December financial year with the standard April–March fiscal year, use the following conversion: \nA calendar year (e.g., January–December 2023) corresponds to the subsequent fiscal year (e.g., FY 2023–24, covering April 2023 to \nMarch 2024). Apply this rule consistently to all such conversions. \n8) \n****Financial turnover in INR/converted equivalent INR of previous financial years shall be given a weightage of 5% per year \n(compounded annually) to bring them to the price level of the Financial Year of this Tender Invitation. \n9) \nAll the documents or certifications, which are provided by Chartered Accountant after 1st July, 2019, must contain UDIN thereon and \nthe particulars of certifications must be same as mentioned on document/certification and submitted to ICAI on its website which can be \nverified online on https://udin.icai.org/search-udin. \n3.2 BID CAPACITY: \nRequirement \nDocument Submission \nRequirement \nAvailable Bid capacity should be ≥ ₹ 4.74 Crores \nFormula: \nAvailable Bid Capacity = (1.5 × A × N) – B  \nAttachment-7, Attachment-\n8 to Letter of Technical Bid"

(ii) \nTenderer as a Prime Contractor (Single entity or Joint Venture member) during last 07(seven) \nyears ending as on last day of the month previous to the month of invitation of this tender, \nshould have completed/ **substantially completed Two works of *Similar nature, where the \nvalue of each work is equal to or exceed ₹ 2.37 Crores. *** \nAttachment-5 & Attachment-\n6 to Letter of Technical Bid \nOR \n3.1.A. (iii) Tenderer as a Prime Contractor (Single entity or Joint Venture member) during last 07(seven) \nyears ending as on last day of the month previous to the month of invitation of this tender, \nshould have completed/ **substantially completed Three works of *Similar nature, where the \nvalue of each work is equal to or exceed ₹ 1.90 Crores.*** \nAttachment-5 & Attachment-\n6 to Letter of Technical Bid \nOR \n3.1.A. (iv) Tenderer as a Prime Contractor (Single entity or Joint Venture member) during last 07(seven) \nyears ending as on last day of the month previous to the month of invitation of this tender, \nAttachment-5 & Attachment-\n6 to Letter of Technical Bid"

Financial    Annual Turnover from    Multipl    Updated Annual\n          No     Year            all classes of civil       ying         Turnover\n                                    engineering          factor\n                               construction works only\n                                    INR                          INR\n                                                   (a)                  (b)             (a)x(b)\n             1    2021-2022                               1.28\n\n             2                  2022-2023                               1.22\n\n             3                  2023-2024                               1.16\n\n             4    2024-2025                               1.10\n             5    2025-2026                               1.05\n\n\n\nNote:\n         1.  Annual  financial statements (Audited Balance sheets including  all related notes and income\n           statements) for last five financial years (2021-22 to 2025-26) shall be submitted by the Tenderer.\n\n         2.  The financial information/Annual Turnover ( in all classes of civil engineering construction works\n             only) of the Tenderer must be certified either by the Independent Financial Auditor (statutory\n            Auditor) of the company appointed under the Companies’ Act or by a Chartered Accountant with his\n          stamp and signature with membership number and firm registration number.\n\n         3.  In case any discrepancy in data is found between the Audited Balance sheet and the financial\n            information/Annual Turnover (n all classes of civil engineering construction works only) submitted,\n            the data as available in the Audited Balance sheet will be considered.\n\n         4.  In case Audited Balance sheet of the last Financial Year ending with 2025-26 is not made available\n          by the Bidder, he must submit an affidavit certifying that 'The Balance Sheet has actually not been\n            audited so far'. In such a case the financial data of previous '4' audited Financial Years will be taken\n              into consideration for evaluation.\n\n         5.  To align a January–December financial year with the standard April–March fiscal year, use the\n             following conversion:\n\n        A calendar year (e.g., January–December 2023) corresponds to the subsequent fiscal year (e.g.,\n         FY 2023–24, covering  April 2023  to March 2024). Apply  this  rule  consistently  to  all such\n            conversions.\n\n         6.   All documents shall reflect the stand-alone financial status of the Tenderer and not the Tenderer’s\n            parent companies, subsidiaries, or affiliates.\n\n         7.   All the documents or certifications, which are provided by CA after 1st July, 2019, must contain\n         UDIN  thereon  and  the  particulars  of  certifications  must  be  same  as  mentioned  on\n            document/certification and submitted to ICAI on  its website which can be  verified online on\n             https://udin.icai.org/search-udin.\n\n\n\n  (Signature) ……………………                           (Signature & Seal) ……………………\n\n  Name of signatory: ………                     Name of signatory: …………………..\n\n  Capacity of signatory: ………………….. [[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol2/vol2_part4B#Employer Requirement, Scope of Work and Technical Specifications – Part 4B: Specifications for Rehabilitation and Restoration Works|Employer Requirement, Scope of Work and Technical Specifications – Part 4B: Specifications for Rehabilitation and Restoration Works]]

>   "text": "180\n       BMRCL/Phase-3/JPN-MRS/Demolition/DLN-P1/2026/157       Employer Requirement, Scope of Work &\n                                                                              Technical Specifications\n\n\n    PART – B: SPECIFICATIONS FOR REHABILITATION AND RESTORATION WORKS\n\n      Restoration works for safety reasons.\n       1.    The BMRCL may appoint consultant/Engineer to conduct Building Condition Study (BCS)\n          and suggest sequence and methodology of demolition including remedial measures\n             required to be undertaken prior to demolition and/or during demolition and/or post\n             demolition.\n                    It is anticipated that, certain structures will be required to be constructed for safety and\n              functional reasons as a result of Building Condition Study. The structures anticipated are\n               front walls, doors, windows, beams and columns etc.\n          The BMRCL has identified few items which are to be executed in this contract. These\n            items  shall be as per KPWD Common Schedule  of Rates  for the year 2023-24.\n           Measurements will be recorded for only those buildings completed under the supervision\n              of consultant/Engineer appointed for Building Condition Study.\n       2.      All Standards, Technical Specifications and Codes of Practice referred to shall be latest\n             editions including all applicable official amendments and revisions. The contractor shall\n         make available at site all relevant KPWD Specifications and Indian Standard Codes of\n             practice as applicable.\n              In case of discrepancy among Standard codes of practice, Technical Specifications and\n             provisions in Sub clauses in this ‘Employer Requirement, Scope of Work & Technical\n              Specifications’, the order of precedence will be as below:\n\n                               i)  Provision in this ‘Employer Requirement, Scope of Work & Technical\n                    Specifications’\n                                 ii)  Technical Specifications\n                                  iii) KPWD Specifications\n                    v) MORTH Specifications\n                           vii) Standard Codes of Practice\n\n       3.    The utilities which are not to be diverted but require supporting, proper supporting be done\n           so that they are not damaged along their branches. All Precautions shall be taken while\n            handling the utilities. The Contractor shall be liable for any damages in this behalf.\n       4.    Before carrying out the work at site, necessary permissions as required from various local\n            agencies / authorities shall be required to be obtained by the contractor. The Employer\n              shall assist only by way of issue of necessary support letters.\n       5.    The work has to be executed carefully without damaging the existing surface/over\n            ground/underground utilities. The contractor shall execute electrical and plumbing works\n            through Licensed Electrical/Plumbing contractors.\n       6.    The Contractor shall strictly adhere to the working drawings or detail drawings and written\n              instructions of the Engineer.\n\n     TECHNICAL SPECIFICATIONS\n\n       1.    MATERIALS AND WORKMANSHIP:     The whole of the materials used on the work\n               shall be new and of the best quality of their respective kind. Other articles, tools, plants\n               shall be the best of the several kinds available in the market and shall be used in the best,\n           most workman like, and most substantial manner to the complete satisfaction of the\n             Engineer.\n           The workmanship is to be the best available and of a high standard. The Contractor shall\n             take all steps immediately to make up deficiency if any noticed by the Engineer. Use must\n           be made of a special tradesman in all aspects of the work and allowances must be made\n                in the rates for the same.\n\n              Contractor shall maintain uniform quality and consistency in workmanship throughout the\n             execution of the work.\n\n\n       Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.                 September 2026           Section Page 30 of 37",

### J1b63f38b8c09440d

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part1#Safety, Health and Environment Manual – Part I: SHE Management|Safety, Health and Environment Manual – Part I: SHE Management]]

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n207\n          11.2.2    This Monthly SHE Audit Rating Score (MARS) report will enable the Employer to\n                   evaluate the general compliance by the Contractor with the Conditions of Contract, the\n                  Employer’s Project SHE Manual and the Contractor’s site specific SHE Plan.\n\n\n          11.2.3   Monthly Audits  will be conducted in accordance with BMRC Guidelines.  The\n                    Project Manager accompanied by the Employer’s representatives shall carry out\n                    the Audit. The Contractor’s senior manager and SHE in-charge should also be\n                      invited to attend.\n\n\n          11.2.4   Timing\n\n\n                The Monthly Audit Rating Score (MARS) should be conducted at least 7 days\n                       prior to the scheduled date of Monthly SHE Committee meeting.\n\n\n          11.2.5   Evaluation\n\n\n          11.2.5.1  The numerical scoring has been weighed on a 1-10 scale. The audit team will use\n                        their observations noted in evaluating the points to be awarded against each of\n                    the elements of the audited section. Wherever some topics and sub-topics are not\n                    applicable the score rating need not be given. The overall audit ratings shall be\n                  achieved by:\n\n\n                    Overall Audit rating  =    Actual Score Achieved   X 100\n\n                                  Maximum Possible Score\n\n\n          11.2.5.2  The criticality of the required actions for the respective sections of the Audit will be\n                      classified as:\n\n\n                          Sl.   Score          Description                          Action\n                   No.\n\n                 1    < 60%   Immediate               Require Contractor to rectify within 24\n                                                          hours\n\n                 2    < 75%   Improvement             Contractor rectification within 7 days and\n                                Necessary               confirmed in writing to Employer\n\n                 3    < 90%   Improvement Desirable    Contractor rectification within one month\n                                                    and confirmed in writing to Employer\n\n\n          11.2.6   Report\n\n              A copy of each Audit Report will be sent to Employer and to all subcontractors,\n                     with whom  it  will then be discussed in detail at the Monthly SHE Committee\n                  Meeting in order to ensure that any corrective actions are agreed upon.\n\n\n          11.3     Monthly Electrical Safety Audit\n\n\n          11.3.1   A team comprising of contractor’s senior SHE (Electrical) engineer and Employer’s\n                    representative shall conduct monthly electrical safety audit covering the following and\n                  submit the report to Employer.\n\n\n                                 i)     Electrical accidents investigation findings and remedy\n\n                                    ii)   Adequacy of power generation and power requirements\n\n                                     iii)   Power distribution and transmission system in place\n\n                          iv)   Updated electrical single line diagram showing the current condition of power\n                        source and distribution including the IP44 DBs arrangement.\n\n                      v)     Electrical protection devices – selection, installation and maintenance.\n\n                          vi)   Earth or ground connection and earth pit maintenance details\n\n\n\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 19 of 114",

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n203\n          7.6      Co-contractors’ participation\n\n\n          7.6.1      In case of depot, station and other contiguous areas where more than one main\n                    contractors are working together, the Employer shall instruct the other contractors to\n                        join for the monthly SHE committee meeting of the main civil contractor, so as to\n                   discuss and decide about the common provision of security, lighting, toilet, drinking\n                   water etc. and sharing the maintenance cost of the same etc.\n\n\n          7.6.2    The general principle for sharing the cost shall be either based on the contract\n                  value of works executed at the contiguous area or the daily average number of\n               workmen employed by each contractor in the contiguous area.\n\n\n          7.7     Minimum time between two monthly SHE Committee meetings\n\n\n          7.7.1    A minimum period of 21 days shall be maintained between any two SHE monthly\n                  committee meetings.\n\n\n          7.8     Agenda\n\n\n          7.8.1    The Secretary shall circulate the agenda of the meeting at least seven working days in\n                 advance of the scheduled date of the meeting to all members.\n\n\n          7.8.2    The agenda should broadly cover the following:\n\n\n                                 i)     Confirmation of minutes\n\n                                    ii)    Chairman’s review/overview of site SHE performance / condition\n\n                                     iii)    Previous month SHE statistics\n\n                          iv)    Incident and Accident Investigation / dangerous occurrence / near miss report\n\n                      v)    Site SHE inspection\n\n                          vi)    Sub-contractors’ SHE issues\n\n                             vii)   Safety presentation by Members\n\n                               viii)  Report from Employer\n\n                          ix)   Matters arising\n\n                      x)   Any other business\n\n\n          7.9      Minutes of the meeting\n\n\n          7.9.1    The Minutes of the meeting shall be prepared as per the format provided at Form\n                   No.: SF- 002 and sent to all members within 2 working days preferably by mail/fax\n                    followed by hardcopy. Safety Committee meeting minutes shall also be displayed in\n                    the notice board for wider publicity to all concerned.\n\n\n          7.10     Disciplinary Action\n\n\n          7.10.1   The chairman shall inform the members of any outstanding issues in the meeting and\n                        in case of repeated offence/ non-compliance by some members or other co/sub\n                    contractors and propose suitable disciplinary action including provisions of monitory\n                    penalty as per the relevant contract clauses, the Employer shall ensure that the same\n                          is implemented.\n\n\n          8.0      ID Card and First day at work, SHE orientation training\n\n\n          8.1     The Contractor shall ensure that all personnel working at the site receive an induction\n             SHE training explaining the nature of the work, the hazards that may be encountered\n                    during the site work and the particular hazards attached to their own function within\n\n\n\n\n\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. >   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n205\n                 marshals shall also be conducted to all foremen/ workmen who were associated\n                   to the concerned jobs.\n\n\n          9.10     Every employee including workman shall take safety Oath daily without fail.\n\n\n          9.11      All vehicle drivers including heavy vehicle operators  shall be trained on\n                  defensive driving at Central Training Institute KSRTC, Shanthinagar Bangalore,\n                  or any other driving institute registered under Motor Vehicles Act.\n\n          9.12       All the above listed training programmes except at clause 9.11 shall be organised by\n                    the contractor only after taking approval from the Employer for the training faculty /\n                     organisation, content and durations.\n\n\n          9.13      In case of failure on the part of the contractor to provide  all the above-\n                mentioned training programs to  all employees in time, the same shall be\n                 provided by  the  Employer  through  accredited  agencies   if  required  by\n                  formulating a common scheme to all contractors. Any administrative expenses\n               and training fee towards the same shall be at the cost of the contractor.\n\n\n          10.0    SHE Inspection\n\n\n          10.1     The contractor shall evolve and administer a system of conducting SHE inspections\n                 and other risk management analysis on a periodical basis.\n\n\n          10.2     The purpose of SHE inspection is to identify any variation in construction activities and\n                    operations, machineries, plant and equipment and processes against the SHE Plan\n                 and its supplementary procedures and programs.\n\n\n          10.3      Following SHE inspections program shall be adopted.\n\n                                 i)    Planned General Inspection\n\n                                    ii)    Routine Inspection\n\n                                     iii)    Specific Inspection\n\n                          iv)   Other Inspection\n\n\n          10.3.1   Planned General Inspection\n\n\n          10.3.1.1  Planned general inspections are performed at predetermined intervals and  it usually\n                    involves the representation from both Contractor and the Employer.\n\n\n          10.3.1.2  Inspections that will be classified under this inspection program are:\n\n                                 i)    Monthly contractor and sub-contractors site safety committee Inspection.\n\n                                    ii)    Weekly safety inspection by construction supervisors (Contractors and Sub-\n                            contractors).\n\n                                     iii)    Daily safety inspection by contractor site SHE team.\n\n\n          10.3.2    Routine Inspection\n\n\n          10.3.2.1  Routine inspections are often referring to the inspection of work site, equipment and\n                  temporary structures performed by site and equipment operators and temporary\n                     structure erectors.\n\n                    Inspections that will be classified under this inspection program are:\n\n                                 i)     Daily Inspection of plant and equipment by operator\n\n                                    ii)    Weekly Inspection of scaffold by scaffolding supervisor\n\n                                     iii)   Monthly Inspection of electrical hand tools by competent electrical supervisor\n\n                          iv)    Quarterly Inspection of temporary electrical systems by competent electrical\n                          supervisor\n\n\n\n\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Any administrative expenses \nand training fee towards the same shall be at the cost of the contractor. \n \n10.0  \nSHE Inspection \n \n10.1 \nThe contractor shall evolve and administer a system of conducting SHE inspections \nand other risk management analysis on a periodical basis. \n \n10.2 \nThe purpose of SHE inspection is to identify any variation in construction activities and \noperations, machineries, plant and equipment and processes against the SHE Plan \nand its supplementary procedures and programs. \n \n10.3 \nFollowing SHE inspections program shall be adopted. \ni) \nPlanned General Inspection \nii) \nRoutine Inspection \niii) \nSpecific Inspection \niv) \nOther Inspection \n \n10.3.1 \nPlanned General Inspection \n \n10.3.1.1  Planned general inspections are performed at predetermined intervals and it usually \ninvolves the representation from both Contractor and the Employer. \n \n \n \n10.3.1.2   Inspections that will be classified under this inspection program are: \ni) \nMonthly contractor and sub-contractors site safety committee Inspection. \nii) \nWeekly safety inspection by construction supervisors (Contractors and Sub-\ncontractors).  \niii) \nDaily safety inspection by contractor site SHE team. \n \n10.3.2  \nRoutine Inspection \n \n10.3.2.1  Routine inspections are often referring to the inspection of work site, equipment and \ntemporary structures performed by site and equipment operators and temporary \nstructure erectors. \nInspections that will be classified under this inspection program are: \ni) \nDaily Inspection of plant and equipment by operator \nii) \nWeekly Inspection of scaffold by scaffolding supervisor \niii) \nMonthly Inspection of electrical hand tools by competent electrical supervisor \niv) \nQuarterly Inspection of temporary electrical systems by competent electrical \nsupervisor \n"

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          204\n          the  operation. The  training  shall cover the contents as given  in the General\n           Instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/004.\n\n\n8.2        All personnel shall be issued a photo identity card of size 85mm x 55mm duly\n        signed by the authorized representative of the contractor before they are\n        engaged for any work as per the format given in the General Instruction\n       BMRC/SHE/CEO/005\n\n\n8.3       Contractor shall also issue a personnel SHE handbook in a language known to the\n          workers, which provides information on SHE and emergency procedures that  all\n         personnel working on  contract are required  to know and the need  to  follow.\n          Contractor shall ensure that this  is distributed and  its content introduced to  all\n         personnel working at the site.\n\n\n9.0     SHE Training\n\n\n9.1     The behaviour of people at all levels of the contractor is critical for SHE performance.\n\n\n9.2     The contractor shall organise quality SHE training to engage Managers, supervisors\n        and other personnel in behavioural change and improve safety performance.\n\n\n9.3     The Contractor shall analyse the training requirements for  all the employees and\n             initiate a  training program  to demonstrate  that  all persons employed,  including\n          subcontractors, are suitably qualified, competent and fit. This will include:\n\n\n                i)     Detailed Job  descriptions  for  all personnel,  to include  their  specific SHE\n                  responsibilities\n\n                  ii)    Specification of qualifications, competency and training requirements for  all\n               personnel\n\n                  iii)   Assessment and  recording  of  training needs  for  all  personnel,  including\n                subcontractors’ employees in the workforce, vendor representatives and site\n                   visitors\n\n             iv)   A system for assessing new hirers e.g. previous training\n\n           v)   A means of confirming that the system is effective\n\n             vi)   A matrix and schedule of training requirements, covering general, task–specific\n             and SHE-related training, showing the training frequency and interval between\n                refresher courses\n\n              vii)   Timely, competent delivery of training courses\n\n\n9.4     The contractor  shall arrange behavioural-based  training programmes  for  all the\n          executives to identify, recognise and eliminate unsafe act and unsafe conditions.\n\n\n9.5     The minimum Employer’s requirement of training needs for various categories of\n        employees are given in general instruction BMRC/SHE/CEO/006\n\n\n9.6     The contents of SHE training to Managers/Supervisors as given in general instruction\n       BMRC/SHE/CEO/007 shall be conducted.\n\n\n9.7     The refresher-training programme to all employees shall be conducted once in\n          six months.\n\n\n9.8      Toolbox talk as given in the Employer’s Project SHE manual shall be conducted\n          to all high-risk workmen everyday.\n\n\n9.9      On-the spot practical  skill development training on height safety including\n         scaffold safety, crane safety, welding safety, electrical safety, traffic safety for\n\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. >   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          206\n           v)    Half-yearly inspection of  lifting machinery,  lifting appliances, equipment and\n              gears by Govt. approved competent person.\n\n10.3.2.2  The list mentioned above is not exhaustive. Contractor may add additional categories.\n          Contractors’ Site SHE Manager will ensure that a system of routine inspections are\n          carried out  periodically  to  all  plants, equipment, powered  tools and any other\n         temporary structures that will pose a hazard to operators and workmen.\n\n\n10.3.3    Specific Inspection\n\n\n10.3.3.1  Specific  inspections  are performed on  activities  without a predetermined  date.\n        Competent supervisors usually perform inspections for ensuring an activity whether it\n             is executed in accordance to a general set of rules; method statement submitted or\n         developed procedures.\n\n\n        The following are examples that will be commonly performed as required on the\n          construction site:\n\n\n                i)     Inspection performed before a heavy lifting operation.\n\n                  ii)    Inspection performed before and after the entry of person into a confined space.\n\n                  iii)    Inspection performed before and after a welding and gas cutting operation.\n\n             iv)    Inspection of formwork before concreting by formwork erector.\n\n\n        The list mentioned above is not exhaustive. The contractor shall ensure that a\n         competent supervisor inspects all high-risk processes and activities.\n\n\n10.3.4   Other Inspection\n\n         Other inspections include the following:\n\n                i)    Mandatory Inspections by Labour Department of Government.\n\n                  ii)   BMRC site SHE management team\n\n\n10.3.5   The contractor shall prepare  all required safety inspection checklist for  all activity\n          operations and equipment. Checklists will be prepared based on the Indian standards,\n          rules and regulations and Employer’s requirements. The formats provided  in the\n          Project SHE manual may be referred.\n\n\n10.3.6     All inspection records and reports will be properly kept and filed for audit purpose.\n          Inspection reports of Planned General Inspection and Routine Inspection will be used\n            for discussion during Safety Committee Meetings.\n\n\n11.0    SHE Audit\n\n\n11.1     General\n\n\n11.1.1   The purpose and scope of SHE audit is to assess potential risk, liabilities and the\n         degree of compliance of construction Safety, Health and Environmental plan and its\n         supplementary  procedures and programs  against  applicable and  current SHE\n           legalisation regulations and requirements of the employer.\n\n\n11.1.2    Project Manager holds the ultimate responsibility in ensuring implementation of SHE\n          audit program during the construction work.\n\n\n11.2     Monthly Audit Rating Score (M A R S)\n\n\n11.2.1   Monthly Audit Rating Score (MARS) will be performed once in a month. A team\n         consisting of Project manager and Employer representative based on the pre-\n        designed score-rating format will conduct  it. The details of the pre-designed\n        monthly audit score rating formats are given in the Project SHE manual.\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 18 of 114",

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n247\n                    monitoring and inspection programs.\n\n          40.12.2   In  Site  Environmental  Plan,  the  Contractor  shall  prepare and submit monthly\n                   Environmental Quality Management Reports in accordance with Requirements as per\n                    Contract.\n\n          40.12.3  The monthly report shall include (but not limited to) the following:\n                       Executive Summary\n\n                       Brief mention of construction activities\n\n                       Monitoring results under AMCP, and NMCP\n\n                       Interpretation of monitoring results, significance and influencing factors\n\n                       Graphical representation of monitored results over past four reporting periods.\n\n                      Measures to control spill under SPCP.\n\n                       Action taken on recommendations under site inspection programme or specific\n                          directions.\n\n                      Summary of complaints, results of investigations and follow-up action\n\n                       Future key issues.\n\n         40.13   COMPLAINT RESPONSE PROCESS\n          40.13.1   Inquiries, complaints and requests for information can be expected from a wide range\n                      of  individuals and organizations both private and government.  The majority of\n                   complaints is likely to be received by BMRCL, although the site offices are also likely\n                      to be contacted.\n\n          40.13.2  The objective of complaint process is to ensure that public and agency complaints are\n                  addressed and resolved consistently and expeditiously.\n\n          40.13.3  The Contractor’s Site Manager will be notified immediately on receipt of complaint that\n              may relate to environmental impacts. The Site Manager will immediately inform the\n                  Engineer and through him the BMRCL.\n\n          40.13.4   Field investigation should determine whether the complaint has merit, and if so action\n                   should be taken to address the impact.\n          40.13.5  The outcome of the investigation and the action taken shall be documented on a\n                   complaint Performa prepared by the Contractor and approved by the Engineer in\n                 advance of the works.\n\n          40.13.6  Where possible, a formal response to each complaint received shall be prepared by\n                    the Contractor within seven days in order to notify the concerned person(s) that action\n                 has been taken.\n\n         40.14   COMPLETION OF THE EQM PROGRAMME\n          40.14.1  The construction of Bangalore Metro  will be undertaken as a series of individual\n                    construction contracts with necessarily different construction program and completion\n                    dates.\n\n          40.14.2  The Engineer shall maintain an overview of the ‘impact causing potential’ of each site\n                     or contract and monitoring parameter with a view to maintaining the most cost\n                      effective use of the environmental resources dedicated to the Project.\n\n          40.14.3 Termination of EQM should focus on the percentage contract completion status and on\n                  the basis of a history of environmental impact arising from the site over a representative\n                 period of monitoring.\n\n         40.13.5    Justifiable application for termination of EQM shall be put forward by the\n                    Contractor  to the Engineer, as necessary throughout the  construction\n                       period.\n\n\n\n\n\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 59 of 114",

>   "text": "Pneumatic Tools                                          85\n          Scraper                                                 85\n            Tractor                                                  84\n\n\n         Noise emission limits apply to equipment used at surface of the construction site during Night\n                    time hours of 9 p.m. to 6 a.m.\n\n      43.2.19     The adjustments for close in equipment noise measurement shall\n                 be made in accordance with Table-4.\n\n                                    TABLE – 4\n              ADJUSTMENTS FOR CLOSE-IN EQUIPMENT NOISE MEASUREMENTS\n                    (Measurement Values to be subtracted from Measured Sound)\n         Distance (Feet)                      Level to Estimate Sound Level at 50 Feet dB (A)\n              19-21                                               8\n              22-23                                               7\n              24-26                                               6\n              27-29                                               5\n              30-33                                               4\n              34-37                                               3\n              38-42                                               2\n              43-47                                               1\n              48-50                                               0\n\n                                       TABLE- 5.\n                          CONSTRUCTION VIBRATION LIMITS\n                             VIBRATION TYPE AND PERMISSIBL\n       AGGREGATE DURATION            LIMIT\n           Sustained (1 hr/day)                               0.01 in/sec (80 VdB re 10-6 in/sec)\n           Transient (<1 hr/day)                               0.03 in/sec (90 VdB re 10-6 in/sec)\n           Transient (<10 min/day)                            0.10 in/sec (100 VdB re 10-6 in/sec)\n\n\n          43.2.20  When  Diesel Generator (DG) Sets  are used  for  operation  of equipment and\n                   machinery, then ‘Standards and Guidelines  for  control  of Noise  Pollution from\n                    Stationery DG Sets’, under Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 shall apply.\n         43.2.21  Should the impact monitoring record noise levels which are:\n                         indicative of a deteriorating situation such that closer monitoring is reasonably\n                            indicated, or\n                        when in the opinion of the Engineer additional measurements are required in\n                        view of deteriorating noise environment, then, the Engineer may require the\n                         Contractor to increase the frequency of impact monitoring at any one or more of\n                          the monitoring stations until the results indicate an improving and acceptable\n                             level of noise.\n\n        43.2..22    The Contractor  shall submit a copy  of monitoring  results. The  results should\n                    represent  a statistical evaluation of data for evaluation of trends and comparison\n                      with noise emission standards.\n\n        43.2.23   Where the Engineer determines that the recorded Noise level is significantly\n                    greater than the acceptable levels, the Engineer may direct the Contractor to\n                   take effective remedial measures including, but not limited to, reviewing noise\n                  sources and modifying working procedures.\n\n         43.2.23    The Contractor shall inform the Engineer of all steps taken to investigate cause of\n                  exceedance and immediate action taken to avoid further exceedance through\n                       written reports and proposals for action under an Event Contingency Plan.\n\n          43.3       Control Requirements\n\n\n          43.3.1     Construction material should be operated and transported in such a manner as not to\n                     create unnecessary noise as outlined below:\n\n\n                                 i)    Perform Work within the procedures outlined herein and comply with applicable\n                        codes,  regulations, and  standards  established by  the  Central and  State\n                     Government and their agencies."

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                          252\n43.2.10  The Engineer shall monitor Contractor’s performance of tasks specified, and  will\n          inspect necessary records, reports and procedures related to the control of noise.\n\n43.2.11  Impact monitoring shall be carried out at noise sensitive receptor locations within 200\n           feet of the construction site once each week and after a change in construction\n            activity. Construction noise measurements shall coincide with daytime and nighttime\n          periods of maximum noise generating construction activities.\n\n43.2.12  Noise Monitoring data will be submitted in a Noise Measurement Report Form. It will\n          contain the type of measurement, duration of measurement, distance of monitoring\n         from construction site, and construction equipment working during monitoring period.\n\n43.2.13   appropriate  parameter  for measuring  construction  noise  impacts  shall be  the\n          equivalent A-weighted sound pressure level (Leq) measured in decibels (dB). The two\n            statistical sound levels L10 and L90; the level exceeded for 10 and 90 percent of the time\n           respectively, shall also be recorded during monitoring. The L90 may be considered as\n          the ambient level into which the L10 as average peak level intrudes. The Lmax, Leq, L10\n        and L90 values will be reported in the noise measurement form along with allowable\n         noise limit. The duration of monitoring shall be for a minimum of 30 minutes.\n\n43.2..14  In no case  shall the Contractor expose the public  to construction noise levels\n         exceeding 90dBA (slow) or to impulsive noise levels with a peak sound pressure level\n         exceeding 140dB as measured on an impulse sound level meter.\n\n43.2.15   Limit for construction noise is based on the existing ambient noise levels in areas\n          adjoining the construction sites.\n\n43.2.16 The noise levels emanating from any source during construction, shall not exceed 5\n         dB(A) or more above existing ambient pre-construction noise levels when measured at\n        a point outside the premises of the location of source. The same may be varied from\n         time to time by and at the sole discretion of the Engineer.\n43.2.17  Where there are no ambient noise measurements, the construction activities shall be\n           limited to levels measured at a distance of 200 feet from the construction limits or at\n          the nearest affected building, whichever is closer, as given in Table-2.\n                                 TABLE-2\n                  ALLOWABLE CONSTRUCTION NOISE\n     LAND USE               MAXIMUM NOISE LEVELS- Lmax dB (A)\n                                            Day Time Night Time\n          Residential                      75             65\n          At all Times\n          Commercial                                   85\n             Industrial                                     90\n\n\n43.2.18   At the surface of the construction site during night time hours, the Contractor shall use\n          only equipment that operating under full load meets the noise limits specified in Table-\n           3, if a sensitive receptor would be affected.\n                             TABLE-3\n NOISE EMISSION LIMITS FOR CONSTRUCTION EQUIPMENT USED DURING NIGHTTIME\n              HOURS; MEASURED AT 50 FEET FROM CONSTRUCTION EQUIPMENT*\n Equipment Category                                     Lmax Level dB(A)\n\n Backhoe                                                80\n Bar Bender                                              75\n Chain Saw                                              81\n Compactor                                              80\n Compressor                                             80\n Concrete Mixer                                           85\n Concrete Pump                                           82\n Crane                                                  85\n Dozer                                                  85\n Front End Loader                                         80\n Generator                                               82\n Gradall                                                 85\n Grader                                                  85\n Paver                                                  85\n\n\n\nBangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd.              September 2026     Section Page 64 of 114",

>       "text": "47.0 ENVIORNMENTAL MANAGEMENT\n\n             47.1 ENVIRONMENTAL MONITORING\n\n              47.1.1 The  Contractor’s  Environmental  Team  shall  carry  out  the  monitoring  of\n                     environmental impacts during construction. Representative sensitive receivers in the\n                           vicinity of the works shall be monitored for noise and air quality impacts.\n              47.1.2  For carrying out impact monitoring for noise and air, equipment shall be provided,\n                    operated and maintained by the Contractor. The equipment shall be kept in a good\n                       state  of  repair  in accordance  with  the  manufacturer’s recommendations and\n                    maintained in proper working order with sufficient spare equipment available in the\n                     event of breakdown to maintain the planned monitoring program.\n              47.1.2 The calibration of monitoring instruments and their respective calibrators shall be\n                       carried out in accordance with the manufacturer’s requirements to ensure they\n                    perform to the same level of accuracy as stated in the manufacturer’s specifications.\n              47.1.3 Suspended Particulate Matter (SPM) levels shall be measured by following the\n                     standard high volume sampling method as set out in High Volume Method for\n                  Suspended Particulate, BIS: 5182-1981\n              47.1.4  24-hour average SPM concentration shall be measured by drawing air through a\n                    High Volume Sampler (HVS) fitted with pre-weighted Glass Fiber filter paper at an\n                   average flow rate not less than 1.1m3 per minute.\n              47.1.5 The minimum requirements to the specifications of sound level meter    should be\n                   as given in IS: 9779-1981\n              47.1.6  Engineer will undertake baseline monitoring to establish background levels. Action\n                      Level of the Contractor shall be based on the results of baseline monitoring\n                    program, which will be made available to him prior to start of construction.\n               47.1.7 The Contractor’s monitoring program is summarized in Table –1.\n\n                                       TABLE-1\n\n                SUMMARY OF CONTRACTOR’S MONITORING PROGRAMME\n                Parameter                   Noise                              Air\n\n          Sampling                Day Time (6.00 to 22.00 hrs):   RSPM, SPM\n                                             Lmax, Leq, L10, L90, L50            24-hours of the day\n                                        Night Time (9 PM – 6AM):      CO: 12 hrs from 8.00 to 20.00\n                                             Lmax, Leq, L10, L90, L50, Ldn          hrs.\n\n\n          Frequency               Once a week (when noise     Two 24-hour Samples every\n           At each location              generating activities are           fifteen days at uniform intervals.\n                                      underway).\n           Locations                To  be  determined  by  the  To be determined by the\n                                        Contractor  based  on  noise  Contractor based on air sensitive\n                                           sensitive receptors.              receptors.\n         Number of Locations        4 Locations                  2 Locations\n           Duration  of  Monitoring by  During Civil Construction        During Civil Construction\n           Contractor\n            Additional Requirements     Adhoc monitoring as required.   Ad hoc monitoring as required\n\n\n        47.2EVENT CONTINGENCY PLAN\n        The Contractor shall prepare an Event Contingency Plan under his Site Environmental Plan. The\n         purpose is to provide, in addition to monitoring activities, procedures for ensuring that  if any\n          environmental  exceedance  of  limiting  values  (either  accidental  or  through  inadequate\n          implementation of mitigation measures on part of the Contractor) does occur, the cause is\n          quickly identified and remedied, and that the risk of a similar event recurring is reduced.\n\n\n          47.3      Air Quality\n\n\n          47.3.1   The  Contractor  shall  take  all necessary  precautions  to minimise  fugitive  dust\n                  emissions from operations involving excavation, grading, and clearing of land and\n                    disposal of waste. He shall not allow emissions of fugitive dust from any transport,\n                    handling, construction or storage activity to remain visible in atmosphere beyond the\n                    property line of emission source for any prolonged period of time without notification to\n                    the Employer."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "text": "47.3.2   The Contractor shall use construction equipment designed and equipped to minimise\n          or control air pollution. He shall maintain evidence of such design and equipment and\n       make these available for inspection by Employer.\n\n\n47.3.3      If  after  commencement  of  construction  activity,  Employer  believes  that  the\n          Contractor’s equipment or methods of working are causing unacceptable air pollution\n         impacts then these shall be inspected and remedial proposals shall be drawn up by\n          the Contractor, submitted for review to the Employer and implemented.\n\n\n47.3.4    In developing these remedial measures, the Contractor shall inspect and review all\n          dust sources that may be contributing to air pollution. Remedial measures include use\n           of additional / alternative equipment by the Contractor or maintenance / modification of\n           existing equipment of the Contractor.\n\n           In the event that approved remedial measures are not being implemented and serious\n         impacts persist, the Employer may direct the Contractor to suspend work until the\n        measures are implemented, as required under the Contract.\n\n\n47.3.5    Contractor’s  transport  vehicles and  other equipment  shall conform  to emission\n         standards  fixed by  Statutory  Agencies  of Government  of  India  or  the  State\n        Government from time to time. The Contractor shall carry out periodical checks and\n         undertake remedial measures including replacement,  if required, so as to operate\n           within permissible norms.\n\n\n47.3.6   The Contractor shall establish and maintain records of routine maintenance program\n            for internal combustion engine powered vehicles and equipment used on this project.\n       He shall keep records available for inspection by Employer.\n\n\n47.3.7   The Contractor shall cover loads of dust generating materials like debris and soil being\n          transported from construction  sites.  All trucks carrying loose material should be\n         covered and loaded with sufficient free- board to avoid spills through the tailboard or\n          sideboards.\n\n\n47.3.8   The Contractor shall promptly transport all excavation disposal materials of whatever\n          kind so as not to delay work on the project. Stockpiling of materials  will only be\n         allowed at sites designated by the Employer. The Contractor shall place excavation\n          materials in the dumping/disposal areas designated in the plans as given in the\n           specifications.\n\n\n47.3.9   The temporary dumping areas shall be maintained by the Contractor at all times until\n          the excavate is re-utilised for backfilling or as directed by Employer. Dust control\n            activities shall continue even during any work stoppage.\n\n\n\n\n47.3.10  The Contractor shall place material in a manner that will minimize dust production.\n          Material shall be minimized each day and wetted, to minimize dust production. During\n          dry weather, dust control methods must be used daily especially on windy, dry days to\n         prevent any dust from blowing across the site perimeter.\n\n\n47.3.11  The Contractor shall water down construction sites as required to suppress dust,\n          during handling of excavation soil or debris or during demolition. The Contractor will\n       make water sprinklers, water supply and water delivering equipment available at any\n         time that it is required for dust control use. Dust screens will be used, as feasible when\n           additional dust  control measures are needed  specially where the work  is near\n          sensitive receptors.\n\n\n47.3.12  The Contractor shall provide a wash pit or a wheel washing and/or vehicle cleaning\n             facility at the exits from work sites such as construction depots and batching plants. At\n         such facility, high-pressure water jets will be directed at the wheels of vehicles to\n        remove all spoil and dirt."

>       "text": "47.3.13  The Contractor shall design and implement his blasting techniques so as to minimise\n                     dust, noise, vibration generation and prevention fly rock.\n\n\n          47.3.14   Blasting technique should be consistent not only with nature and quaintly of rock to be\n                    blasted but also the location of blasting.\n\n          47.3.15  The  contractor  shall  give  preference  to  explosives  with  better  environmental\n                      characteristics.\n\n          47.3.16  The Contractor shall protect structures, utilities, pavements roads and other facilities\n                  from disfiguration and damage as a result of his activities. Where this is not possible,\n                    the contractor  shall restore the structures,  utilities, pavements, roads and other\n                          facilities to their original or better, failing which the rectification/restoration work shall\n                be carried out at the risk and cost of the contractor.\n\n\n          47.3.17  The Contractor shall submit to the Employer an Air Monitoring and Control Plan\n               (AMCP) under contract specific Site Environmental Plan to guide construction activity\n                     insofar as it relates to monitoring, controlling and mitigating air pollution.\n\n\n          47.4    AIR MONITORING\n          47.4.1    Construction activities that will generate dust impacts include excavation (including\n                     related activities), material handling and stockpiling, vehicular movement, and wind\n                   erosion of unpaved work areas.\n\n          47.4.2 The impact of fugitive dust on ambient air pollution depends on the quantity generated, as\n                     well as the drift potential of the dust particles injected into the atmosphere. Large dust\n                      particles will settle out near the source and smaller particles are likely to undergo\n                    dispersal over greater distance from the sources and impeded settling. SPM levels will\n                be monitored to evaluate the dust impact during the construction phase of the Project.\n\n          47.4.3   The  Air  Quality  Monitoring and  Control Plan (AMCP)  in  contract-specific  Site\n                   Environmental Plan prepared by the Contractor shall establish procedures to monitor\n                  impact air quality and measures to control air pollution including dust suppression due\n                      to construction activities at work sites. This plan shall contain description of activities\n                      that  will cause degradation  in  air  quality, environmental procedures  to manage\n                     pollutants to minimise the  air  pollution, monitoring program, record keeping and\n                      reporting.\n\n          47.4.4   The Engineer shall monitor Contractor’s performance of tasks specified, and will inspect\n                  necessary records, reports and procedures related to the control of air quality given in\n               AMCP.\n          47.4.5    Information gathered during the AMCP  will be catalogued and maintained by the\n                    Contractor and shall be available for review by the Engineer.\n\n          47.4.6   The exact location of the air monitoring stations located near air sensitive receptors\n                    adjoining the construction sites, such as residences, schools, hotels and hospitals and\n                  placement of monitoring equipment thereat shall be agreed with the Engineer prior to\n               commencement of air monitoring program.\n\n          47.4.7   Impact monitoring during the course  of the Works  shall be carried out  at the\n                    monitoring stations for two days (continuous twenty-four hours) every fifteen days and\n                 where there is a perceived air quality problem.\n          47.4.8   The Contractor shall construct suitable fence, lockable gate, 220V AC power point and\n                     suitable access at each air monitoring station.  Monitoring stations shall be free from\n                      local obstructions or sheltering.\n\n\n          47.4.9   Should impact monitoring record dust levels which are:\n\n\n                       indicative of a deteriorating situation such that closer monitoring is reasonably\n                          indicated, or\n\n\n                      when in the opinion of the Engineer additional measurements are required in view\n                          of deteriorating air quality,"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 76,
>       "text": "Then the Engineer may require the Contractor to increase the frequency of impact\n          monitoring at any one or more of the monitoring stations until the results indicate an\n         improving and acceptable level of air quality.\n\n\n47.4.10  The Contractor shall keep records of air quality monitoring (including location, date,\n           time). The Contractor shall submit a copy of monitoring results to the Engineer. The\n           results should represent a  statistical evaluation of data by calculating maximum,\n        minimum, mean, standard deviation, geometric mean and percentile calculations for\n          evaluation of frequency distribution, trends, and comparison with emission standards.\n\n\n47.4.11  The National Ambient Air Quality Standards given in Air (Prevention and Control of\n           Pollution) Act, 1981 may be referred by the Contractor for Limit Levels of SPM in\n         ambient  air which may be followed  in estimating the  pollution  level caused by\n          Contractor’s activities.\n\n47.4.12  Where  the  Engineer  determines  that  the  recorded  dust  (TSP)  level  is\n          significantly  greater  than  the  Limit  levels,  the Engineer may  direct  the\n         Contractor to take effective remedial measures including, but not limited to,\n         reviewing dust sources and modifying working procedures.\n\n47.4.13  Where the recorded baseline levels exceed the ambient air quality standards, then at\n         such locations the action level is the recorded base line. Contractor shall take all\n           effective remedial measures to contain the levels to their baseline value as a result of\n           his activities. The action level may be varied by and at the sole discretion of the\n         Engineer.\n\n47.4.14 The Contractor shall inform the Engineer of  all steps taken to investigate cause of\n        exceedance and immediate action taken to avoid further exceedance through written\n         reports and proposals for action under an Event Contingency Plan."
