>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 73,
>       "source_line_number": 55,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 73,
>       "source_line_number": 56,
>       "text": "        47.2EVENT CONTINGENCY PLAN"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 73,
>       "source_line_number": 57,
>       "text": "        The Contractor shall prepare an Event Contingency Plan under his Site Environmental Plan. The"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 73,
>       "source_line_number": 58,
>       "text": "         purpose is to provide, in addition to monitoring activities, procedures for ensuring that  if any"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 73,
>       "source_line_number": 59,
>       "text": "          environmental  exceedance  of  limiting  values  (either  accidental  or  through  inadequate"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 73,
>       "source_line_number": 60,
>       "text": "          implementation of mitigation measures on part of the Contractor) does occur, the cause is"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 73,
>       "source_line_number": 61,
>       "text": "          quickly identified and remedied, and that the risk of a similar event recurring is reduced."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 73,
>       "source_line_number": 62,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 73,
>       "source_line_number": 63,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 73,
>       "source_line_number": 64,
>       "text": "          47.3      Air Quality"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 73,
>       "source_line_number": 65,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 73,
>       "source_line_number": 66,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 73,
>       "source_line_number": 67,
>       "text": "          47.3.1   The  Contractor  shall  take  all necessary  precautions  to minimise  fugitive  dust"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 73,
>       "source_line_number": 68,
>       "text": "                  emissions from operations involving excavation, grading, and clearing of land and"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 73,
>       "source_line_number": 69,
>       "text": "                    disposal of waste. He shall not allow emissions of fugitive dust from any transport,"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 73,
>       "source_line_number": 70,
>       "text": "                    handling, construction or storage activity to remain visible in atmosphere beyond the"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 73,
>       "source_line_number": 71,
>       "text": "                    property line of emission source for any prolonged period of time without notification to"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 73,
>       "source_line_number": 72,
>       "text": "                    the Employer."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 73,
>       "source_line_number": 73,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 73,
>       "source_line_number": 74,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 73,
>       "source_line_number": 75,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 73,
>       "source_line_number": 76,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 3,
>       "text": "47.3.2   The Contractor shall use construction equipment designed and equipped to minimise"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 4,
>       "text": "          or control air pollution. He shall maintain evidence of such design and equipment and"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 5,
>       "text": "       make these available for inspection by Employer."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 6,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 7,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 8,
>       "text": "47.3.3      If  after  commencement  of  construction  activity,  Employer  believes  that  the"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 9,
>       "text": "          Contractor’s equipment or methods of working are causing unacceptable air pollution"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 10,
>       "text": "         impacts then these shall be inspected and remedial proposals shall be drawn up by"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 11,
>       "text": "          the Contractor, submitted for review to the Employer and implemented."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 12,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 13,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 14,
>       "text": "47.3.4    In developing these remedial measures, the Contractor shall inspect and review all"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 15,
>       "text": "          dust sources that may be contributing to air pollution. Remedial measures include use"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 16,
>       "text": "           of additional / alternative equipment by the Contractor or maintenance / modification of"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 17,
>       "text": "           existing equipment of the Contractor."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 18,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 19,
>       "text": "           In the event that approved remedial measures are not being implemented and serious"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 20,
>       "text": "         impacts persist, the Employer may direct the Contractor to suspend work until the"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 21,
>       "text": "        measures are implemented, as required under the Contract."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 22,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 23,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 24,
>       "text": "47.3.5    Contractor’s  transport  vehicles and  other equipment  shall conform  to emission"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 25,
>       "text": "         standards  fixed by  Statutory  Agencies  of Government  of  India  or  the  State"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 26,
>       "text": "        Government from time to time. The Contractor shall carry out periodical checks and"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 27,
>       "text": "         undertake remedial measures including replacement,  if required, so as to operate"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 28,
>       "text": "           within permissible norms."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 29,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 30,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 31,
>       "text": "47.3.6   The Contractor shall establish and maintain records of routine maintenance program"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 32,
>       "text": "            for internal combustion engine powered vehicles and equipment used on this project."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 33,
>       "text": "       He shall keep records available for inspection by Employer."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 34,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 35,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 36,
>       "text": "47.3.7   The Contractor shall cover loads of dust generating materials like debris and soil being"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 37,
>       "text": "          transported from construction  sites.  All trucks carrying loose material should be"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 38,
>       "text": "         covered and loaded with sufficient free- board to avoid spills through the tailboard or"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 39,
>       "text": "          sideboards."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 40,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 41,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 42,
>       "text": "47.3.8   The Contractor shall promptly transport all excavation disposal materials of whatever"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 43,
>       "text": "          kind so as not to delay work on the project. Stockpiling of materials  will only be"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 44,
>       "text": "         allowed at sites designated by the Employer. The Contractor shall place excavation"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 45,
>       "text": "          materials in the dumping/disposal areas designated in the plans as given in the"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 46,
>       "text": "           specifications."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 47,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 48,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 49,
>       "text": "47.3.9   The temporary dumping areas shall be maintained by the Contractor at all times until"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 50,
>       "text": "          the excavate is re-utilised for backfilling or as directed by Employer. Dust control"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 51,
>       "text": "            activities shall continue even during any work stoppage."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 52,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 53,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 54,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 55,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 56,
>       "text": "47.3.10  The Contractor shall place material in a manner that will minimize dust production."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 57,
>       "text": "          Material shall be minimized each day and wetted, to minimize dust production. During"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 58,
>       "text": "          dry weather, dust control methods must be used daily especially on windy, dry days to"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 59,
>       "text": "         prevent any dust from blowing across the site perimeter."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 60,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 61,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 62,
>       "text": "47.3.11  The Contractor shall water down construction sites as required to suppress dust,"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 63,
>       "text": "          during handling of excavation soil or debris or during demolition. The Contractor will"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 64,
>       "text": "       make water sprinklers, water supply and water delivering equipment available at any"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 65,
>       "text": "         time that it is required for dust control use. Dust screens will be used, as feasible when"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 66,
>       "text": "           additional dust  control measures are needed  specially where the work  is near"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 67,
>       "text": "          sensitive receptors."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 68,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 69,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 70,
>       "text": "47.3.12  The Contractor shall provide a wash pit or a wheel washing and/or vehicle cleaning"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 71,
>       "text": "             facility at the exits from work sites such as construction depots and batching plants. At"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 72,
>       "text": "         such facility, high-pressure water jets will be directed at the wheels of vehicles to"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 73,
>       "text": "        remove all spoil and dirt."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 74,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 75,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 76,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 74,
>       "source_line_number": 77,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 3,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 4,
>       "text": "          47.3.13  The Contractor shall design and implement his blasting techniques so as to minimise"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 5,
>       "text": "                     dust, noise, vibration generation and prevention fly rock."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 6,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 7,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 8,
>       "text": "          47.3.14   Blasting technique should be consistent not only with nature and quaintly of rock to be"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 9,
>       "text": "                    blasted but also the location of blasting."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 10,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 11,
>       "text": "          47.3.15  The  contractor  shall  give  preference  to  explosives  with  better  environmental"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 12,
>       "text": "                      characteristics."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 13,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 14,
>       "text": "          47.3.16  The Contractor shall protect structures, utilities, pavements roads and other facilities"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 15,
>       "text": "                  from disfiguration and damage as a result of his activities. Where this is not possible,"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 16,
>       "text": "                    the contractor  shall restore the structures,  utilities, pavements, roads and other"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 17,
>       "text": "                          facilities to their original or better, failing which the rectification/restoration work shall"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 18,
>       "text": "                be carried out at the risk and cost of the contractor."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 19,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 20,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 21,
>       "text": "          47.3.17  The Contractor shall submit to the Employer an Air Monitoring and Control Plan"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 22,
>       "text": "               (AMCP) under contract specific Site Environmental Plan to guide construction activity"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 23,
>       "text": "                     insofar as it relates to monitoring, controlling and mitigating air pollution."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 24,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 25,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 26,
>       "text": "          47.4    AIR MONITORING"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 27,
>       "text": "          47.4.1    Construction activities that will generate dust impacts include excavation (including"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 28,
>       "text": "                     related activities), material handling and stockpiling, vehicular movement, and wind"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 29,
>       "text": "                   erosion of unpaved work areas."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 30,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 31,
>       "text": "          47.4.2 The impact of fugitive dust on ambient air pollution depends on the quantity generated, as"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 32,
>       "text": "                     well as the drift potential of the dust particles injected into the atmosphere. Large dust"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 33,
>       "text": "                      particles will settle out near the source and smaller particles are likely to undergo"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 34,
>       "text": "                    dispersal over greater distance from the sources and impeded settling. SPM levels will"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 35,
>       "text": "                be monitored to evaluate the dust impact during the construction phase of the Project."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 36,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 37,
>       "text": "          47.4.3   The  Air  Quality  Monitoring and  Control Plan (AMCP)  in  contract-specific  Site"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 38,
>       "text": "                   Environmental Plan prepared by the Contractor shall establish procedures to monitor"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 39,
>       "text": "                  impact air quality and measures to control air pollution including dust suppression due"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 40,
>       "text": "                      to construction activities at work sites. This plan shall contain description of activities"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 41,
>       "text": "                      that  will cause degradation  in  air  quality, environmental procedures  to manage"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 42,
>       "text": "                     pollutants to minimise the  air  pollution, monitoring program, record keeping and"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 43,
>       "text": "                      reporting."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 44,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 45,
>       "text": "          47.4.4   The Engineer shall monitor Contractor’s performance of tasks specified, and will inspect"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 46,
>       "text": "                  necessary records, reports and procedures related to the control of air quality given in"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 47,
>       "text": "               AMCP."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 48,
>       "text": "          47.4.5    Information gathered during the AMCP  will be catalogued and maintained by the"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 49,
>       "text": "                    Contractor and shall be available for review by the Engineer."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 50,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 51,
>       "text": "          47.4.6   The exact location of the air monitoring stations located near air sensitive receptors"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 52,
>       "text": "                    adjoining the construction sites, such as residences, schools, hotels and hospitals and"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 53,
>       "text": "                  placement of monitoring equipment thereat shall be agreed with the Engineer prior to"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 54,
>       "text": "               commencement of air monitoring program."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 55,
>       "text": ""
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 56,
>       "text": "          47.4.7   Impact monitoring during the course  of the Works  shall be carried out  at the"
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 75,
>       "source_line_number": 57,
>       "text": "                    monitoring stations for two days (continuous twenty-four hours) every fifteen days and"
>     },

### Jd9da9c7b2d4b3646

[[OKF_bundle/Technical/Vol3/vol3_part4#Clause 48.0 — Water Quality|Clause 48.0 — Water Quality]]

> {
>   "clause_id": "48.0",
>   "fragments": [
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 76,
>       "text": "48.0     Water Quality\n\n\n48.1    The Contractor shall comply with the Indian Government legislation and other State\n          regulations in existence in Delhi insofar as they relate to water pollution control and\n          monitoring. A drainage system should be constructed at the commencement of the\n         Works, to drain off all surface water from the work site into suitable drain outlet.\n\n\n48.2    The Contractor shall provide adequate precautions to ensure that no spoil or debris of\n        any kind is pushed, washed, falls or deposited on land adjacent to the site perimeter\n          including public roads or existing stream courses and drains within or adjacent to the\n            site. In the event of any spoil or debris from construction works being deposited or any\n               silt washed down to any area, then all such spoil, debris or material and silt shall be\n         immediately removed and the affected land and areas restored to their natural state by\n          the Contractor to the satisfaction of the Employer.\n\n\n48.3    Due to lowering of potable water supplies in Bangalore and subsequent contamination\n           of ground water, the Contractor is not allowed to discharge water from the site without\n          the approval of the Employer. The Contractor must comply with the requirements of\n          the Local Ground Water Board for discharge of water arising from dewatering. Any\n         water obtained from dewatering systems installed in the works must be either re-used\n            for construction purposes and this water may subsequently be discharged to the\n         drainage system or,  if not re-used, recharged to the ground water at suitable aquifer\n           levels. The Contractor must submit his proposals for approval of Employer, on his\n         proposed locations of dewatering of excavation and collection of water for either\n          construction re-use  or recharge  directly  to  aquifers. The  Contractor’s recharge\n         proposals must be sufficient for recharging of the quantity of water remaining after\n         deduction of water re-used for construction. During dewatering, the contractor shall\n         monitor ground water levels from wells to ensure that draw down levels do not exceed\n          allowable limits.  The Contractor will not be permitted to directly discharge, to the\n         drainage system, unused ground  water  obtaining  from  the  excavation  without\n          obtaining approval of Employer or the Agency controlling the system."
>     },
>     {
>       "pdf_page": 77,
>       "text": "48.4    The Contractor shall ensure that earth, bentonite, chemicals and concrete agitator\n                  washings etc. are not deposited in the watercourses but are suitably collected and\n                   residue disposed off in a manner approved by local authorities.\n\n\n          48.5       All water and waste products (surface runoff and wastewater) arising on the site shall\n                be  collected and removed from  the  site  via a  suitable and properly designed\n                  temporary drainage system and disposed off at a location and in a manner that will\n                 cause neither pollution nor nuisance.\n\n\n          48.6    Any mud slurry from drilling, tunnelling, diaphragm wall construction or grouting etc.\n                      shall not be discharged into the drainage system unless treatment is carried out that\n                          will remove silt, mud particles, bentonite etc. The Contractor shall provide treatment\n                          facilities as necessary to prevent the discharge of contaminated ground water.\n\n\n          48.7    The Contractor shall discharge wastewater arising out of site office, canteen or toilet\n                          facilities constructed by him into sewers after obtaining prior approval of agency\n                      controlling the system.  A wastewater drainage system shall be provided to drain\n                  wastewater into the sewerage system.\n\n\n          48.8    The bentonite mixing, treatment and handling system shall be established by the\n                     contractor giving due regard to its environmental impacts. The disposal of redundant\n                    bentonite shall be carefully considered whether in bulk or liquid form. The disposal\n                     location will be advised and agreed with the relevant authorities.\n\n\n          48.9    The Contractor shall take measures to prevent discharge of oil and grease during\n                     spillage from reaching drainage system or any water body. Oil removal / interceptors\n                      shall be provided to treat oil waste from workshop areas etc.\n\n         48.10   The Contractor shall apply to the appropriate authority for installing bore wells for\n                   water supply at site."
>     }
>   ],

>   "text": "Safety Health & Environment (SHE) Manual\n                                                            264\n                      PART - V: PENALTY AND AWARDS\n\n\n   56.0     Charges to be recovered from contractor for unsafe act or condition\n\n\n   56.1    BMRC has built an image of safety conscious organisation meticulously over a period\n              of seven years. Any reportable accident (fatality / injury) results in loss of life and/or\n             property damage. These accidents not only result in loss of life but also damage the\n             reputation of BMRC. Most of the accidents are avoidable and caused preliminary due\n              to contractors’ negligence. Hence BMRC shall recover the cost of damages from the\n             contractors for every reportable incident (fatality / injury).\n\n\n   56.2      In addition every BMRC work  site  is exposed to public scrutiny as the work  is\n            executed just on the right-of-way. Any unsafe act  / unsafe condition observed by\n              public further damages our reputation. Because of the non-voluntary compliance of\n             contractors to the condition of contract on SHE and project SHE manual, BMRC has\n           been forced to establish safety-enforcing organisation. The cost of established such\n             organisation is to be recovered from contractors for all observed safety violations at\n               sites.\n\n\n   56.3    The following table indicates the Safety, Health and Environment violation (unsafe act\n                      / unsafe condition) and charges to be recovered from contractors.\n\n\nSL. The\n                 charges shall be in comparison with that of the similar offence indicated in clause\n                     56.3.\n\n\n          57.0     Stoppage of work\n\n\n          57.1    The Employer shall have the right to stop the work at his sole discretion, if in his opinion the\n                 work is being carried out in such a way that  it may cause accidents and endanger the\n                    safety of the persons and / or property, and / or equipments. In such cases, the contractor\n                      shall be informed in writing about the nature of hazards and possible injury / accident.\n\n\n          57.2    The contractor shall not proceed with the work until he has complied with each direction to\n                    the satisfaction of Employer.\n\n          57.3    The Contractor shall not be entitled for any damages / compensation for stoppage of work,\n                due to safety reasons and the period of such stoppage of work shall not be taken as an\n                   extension of time for Completion of the Facilities and will not be the ground for waiver of\n                    levy of liquidated damages.\n\n\n          58.0    Awards\n\n                The following categories will be considered for awards as per the scheme in practice of\n                 Employer\n\n                                 i)    For every safe million man hour working without any reportable incidents\n\n                                    ii)    Zero fatality contracts\n\n                                     iii)   100% adherence to voluntary reporting of all accidents throughout the currency of\n                           contract\n\n                          iv)    Safest project team of the year.\n\n                      v)    Best SHE team of the year.\n\n                          vi)    Safest Contractor of the year.\n\n\n\n         Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. >       "text": "BANGALORE METRO RAIL CORPORATION LTD.\n\n\n\n                                APPENDIX NO.: 4\n\n\n\n        WORKPLACE POLICY ON HIV/AIDS PREVENTION & CONTROL FOR WORKMEN\n                        ENGAGED BY CONTRACTORS\n\n             “Being mobile in and of itself is not a risk factor for HIV infection.  It is the situations\n           encountered and the behaviours possibly engaged in during mobility or migration that\n                           increase vulnerability and risk regarding HIV / AIDS.”\n\n               UNAIDS, Technical update on ‘Population, Mobility and AIDS’, February 2001, p.5\n\n        Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation (BMRC) recognizes HIV  / AIDS as a developmental\n         challenge and realizes the need to respond to  it by implementing regular HIV  / AIDS\n         prevention programmes and  creating a  non-discriminatory work environment  for HIV\n          infected workmen engaged by contractors.  For the purpose of making conscientious,\n          sensitive and compassionate decision in addressing the realities of HIV / AIDS, DMRC has\n         established these guidelines based on ILO code of practice on HIV / AIDS."

> {
>   "pdf_page": 99,
>   "text": "BANGALORE METRO RAIL CORPORATION LTD.\n\n\n\n                            General Instruction: BMRC/SHE/CEO/003\n\n\n\n         SUGGESTIVE REQUIREMENTS OF SHE MONITORING AND AUDIO-VISUAL EQUIPMENTS\n\n\n           1.    For the purpose of minimum requirements of Audio-visual and Other equipment the contracts\n                categorized into the following groups:\n\n\n\n                            Contract Value (Initial awarded value of contract)                 Group\n\n\n                                         Upto 25 Cr                            A\n\n\n                                         Upto 100 Cr                            B\n\n\n                                         Upto 250 Cr                         C\n\n\n                                   More than 250 Cr                        D\n\n\n\n           2.    Every contractor falling into the above groups shall provide the following minimum required\n               audio visual aids for conducting weekly review, monthly safety committee and other post\n               review meeting of all fatal and major incidences effectively. These audio-visual equipments\n               are a must  for  conducting  periodical  in-house  safety  presentations  in  the  training\n              programmes.\n\n           3.     In addition to the above portable hand held digital sound level meter (SLM) and portable hand\n               held digital lux meter are also to be provided.\n\n\n                                        SHE monitoring and Audio-Visual equipment\n                 Sl.   SHE monitoring and Audio-Visual                 required for\n          No          Equipment details        Group A   Group B  Group C    Group D\n                                                     Contract   Contract   Contract     Contract\n\n                 1.  Portable hand held Digital Sound Level\n                                                      1         1         1           1\n                 Meter (SLM)\n\n                 2.  Portable hand held Digital Lux Meter         1         1         1           1\n\n                 3.  Laptop Computer with standard\n                    configuration including multi media          1         1         1           1\n                         facilities\n                 4.  Colour Printer                           1         1         1           1\n\n                 5. Computer projector with screen                      -         1         1           1\n\n                 6. Overhead projector                       1\n                 7. 35mm Camera (For taking accident\n                    investigation photos in which case the        1         1         1           1\n                images can not be easily altered)\n                      Digital camera with flash of minimum 4                 8.                                       1         1         1           2\n              mega pixel and video facility\n                 9.  Digital still camera with flash of             1         2         4           6\n               minimum 4 mega pixel\n\n\n               10. Portable loudspeaker (for tool-box talk\n                                                      1         1         2           6\n                and emergency purpose)\n\n               11. Communication facility like mobile      For all supervisors and managers/engineers working\n                 phone, walky-talky etc                  Safety, Health & Environment"

>       "pdf_page": 20,
>       "text": "18.0     TENDER OPENING\n\n         18.1     The tenders shall be opened online in the eProcurement Portal by the Employer on the\n                  scheduled date and time of tender opening as mentioned in NIT or as per subsequent\n                amendment if any at the office of the General Manager (Contracts) address mentioned in NIT.\n                               (If such scheduled date for opening of Bid is subsequently declared as a Public Holiday by\n                    the Employer, the next official working day shall be deemed to be the date of opening of the\n                      Bids).\n\n         18.2     On opening the technical bid, the tender opening committee will first check the tender security\n                (EMD) documents submitted by the bidder on the eProcurement Portal.\n\n         18.4      Tender  submittals/ documents  of  all  online  bids accepted by the Employer on the\n                  eProcurement Portal shall be downloaded for further technical evaluation.\n\n         18.5     The Financial Bid(s) will be opened on the eProcurement portal on a subsequent date after\n                    the evaluation of technical bids. Financial Bids of only those tenderers whose submissions\n                   are found substantially responsive and technically compliant as per clause 22.1 of ITT will be\n                  opened. The time of opening of financial bids shall be informed through the eProcurement\n                       Portal. Bidders shall visit the eProcurement Portal regularly for updates."
>     }

>       "text": "14         Risk and Responsibility\n\nIndemnity        14.1      The Contractor shall indemnify and hold harmless the Employer, the Engineer, the\n                            Designated Contractors, representatives and employees from and against  all\n                                 actions, suits, proceedings, claims, damages, losses, expenses and demands of\n                             every nature and description, by reasons of any act or omissions of the Contractor,\n                                  his representative or his employees in the execution of the Works, including\n                                professional services provided by the Contractor or in the guarding the same.\n                         These indemnification obligations shall include but not be limited to claims,\n                          damages,  losses, damage proceedings, charges and expenses which are\n                                   attributable to:\n\n                                    (a)   sickness, or disease, or death of, or injury to any person; and\n                                    (b)   loss of, or damage to, or destruction of any property (other than the Works)\n                                       including consequential loss of use; and\n                                     (c)   Loss, damage or costs arising from the carriage of Plant and Materials\n                                     and/or ownership or chartering of marine vessels by the Contractor, or any\n                                      sub-contractor of any tier.\n\n                         The Contractor shall also indemnify and save harmless the Employer from and\n                               against all claims and proceedings on account of infringements of patents rights,\n                               design, trademark name etc. as detailed out in Sub Clause 5.8.\n\n                                      All sums payable by way of compensation under these conditions shall be\n                             considered reasonable compensation payable to the Employer, without reference\n                                  to the actual loss or damage sustained, and whether or not any damage shall have\n                          been sustained. The decision of the Engineer as to compensation claimed shall\n                          be final and binding.\n\nContractor’s      14.2      The Contractor shall take full responsibility for the care of the Works, or any part\nCare of the                     thereof, including full responsibility for the care of any work being manufactured,\nWorks                         or stored off-Site for inclusion in the Works, or in the course of transportation to\n                               the Site, and for the care of Contractor’s Equipment, Temporary Works, Plant and\n                          any other Material, whatsoever, on the Site or delivered to or placed on the Site in\n                             connection with, or for the purpose of the Works.\n\n                         The Contractor shall take this responsibility from the Commencement Date until\n                               the date of issue of the Taking Over Certificate, when responsibility shall pass to\n                               the Employer. If the Engineer issues a Taking Over Certificate for any Section or\n                                 part of the Works, the Contractor shall cease to be responsible for the care of that\n                              Section or part from the date of issue of such Taking Over Certificate when\n                                  responsibility shall pass to the Employer.\n\n                         The Contractor shall take responsibility for the care of any outstanding work which\n                                        is required to be completed prior to the expiry of the Contract Period, until the\n                            Engineer confirms in writing that such outstanding work has been completed.\n                                                   If any loss or damage happens to the Works, any other property or person, arising\n                            from any cause other than the Employer's risks listed in Sub-Clause14.3, during\n                               the period for which the Contractor is responsible, the Contractor shall rectify such\n                                loss or damage, at his cost, so that the Works conform with the Contract or at the\n                               option of the Employer, will pay or allow to the Employer the cost of rectifying such\n                                loss or damage. Notwithstanding such loss or damage, the Contractor shall\n                            proceed with the execution of Works in  all respects in accordance with the\n                              Contract and the Engineer's instructions. The Contractor shall also be liable for\n                          any loss or damage to the Works caused by any operations carried out by the\n                               Contractor after the date of issue of the Taking Over Certificate.\n\nEmployer’s       14.3      The Employer's risks of loss or damage to physical property in India and of death\nRisks                     and personal injury occurring in India in consequence of the performance of\n                                 obligations under the Contract are:\n\n                                    (a)   War, hostilities (whether war be declared or not), invasion, act of foreign\n                                  enemies, act of terrorism.\n                                    (b)    rebellion, revolution, insurrection, or military or usurped power, or civil war,\n                                         within India,"

Conciliation  shall\n                       commence when the other party accepts in writing this invitation.
